#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <limits>
#include <vector>

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// WGS84 Constants & Fundamental Geodesy
// ------------------------------------------------------------
namespace wgs84 {
constexpr double a       = 6378137.0;                          // Semi-major axis (m)
constexpr double f       = 1.0 / 298.257223563;                // Flattening
constexpr double e2      = 2.0 * f - f * f;                    // Eccentricity squared
constexpr double e       = std::sqrt(e2);
constexpr double q_p     = (1.0 - e2) * (std::sin(M_PI_2) / (1.0 - e2) - 
                           std::log((1.0 - e) / (1.0 + e)) / (2.0 * e)); // Authalic q(pi/2)
constexpr double R_aut   = a * std::sqrt(q_p / 2.0);           // Authalic Radius (m) ~ 6371007.181
constexpr double deg2rad = M_PI / 180.0;
constexpr double rad2deg = 180.0 / M_PI;
} // namespace wgs84

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Utility: High-Precision Math Helpers
// ------------------------------------------------------------
inline double clamp(double v, double lo, double hi) {
    return std::max(lo, std::min(hi, v));
}

// Accurate sin/cos for small angles via argument reduction not needed for double here,
// but we guard asin/acos domains.
inline double safe_asin(double x) { return std::asin(clamp(x, -1.0, 1.0)); }
inline double safe_acos(double x) { return std::acos(clamp(x, -1.0, 1.0)); }
inline double safe_sqrt(double x) { return std::sqrt(std::max(0.0, x)); }

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Geodetic -> Authalic Latitude (Equal-Area Sphere Mapping)
// q(phi) = (1-e^2) * ( sin(phi)/(1-e^2 sin^2 phi) - atanh(e sin(phi))/e )
// beta = asin( q(phi) / q_p )
// ------------------------------------------------------------
inline double geodetic_to_authalic_lat(double phi) {
    const double sin_phi = std::sin(phi);
    const double e_sin   = wgs84::e * sin_phi;
    const double denom   = 1.0 - wgs84::e2 * sin_phi * sin_phi;
    
    // q(phi) computation stable for all latitudes
    double q;
    if (std::abs(e_sin) < 1e-12) {
        q = sin_phi; // Limit e->0
    } else {
        q = (1.0 - wgs84::e2) * (sin_phi / denom - std::atanh(e_sin) / wgs84::e);
    }
    return safe_asin(q / wgs84::q_p);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Spherical Trigonometry on Authalic Sphere (Radius R_aut)
// ------------------------------------------------------------
struct SphericalPoint {
    double lat; // Authalic latitude (rad)
    double lon; // Longitude (rad)
};

// Haversine distance (angle) on unit sphere. Returns central angle sigma.
inline double haversine_angle(const SphericalPoint& p1, const SphericalPoint& p2) {
    const double dlat = p2.lat - p1.lat;
    const double dlon = p2.lon - p1.lon;
    const double sin_dlat2 = std::sin(dlat * 0.5);
    const double sin_dlon2 = std::sin(dlon * 0.5);
    const double h = sin_dlat2 * sin_dlat2 + 
                     std::cos(p1.lat) * std::cos(p2.lat) * sin_dlon2 * sin_dlon2;
    return 2.0 * safe_asin(safe_sqrt(h)); // Central angle in radians
}

// Azimuth (forward) at p1 towards p2 on unit sphere. Returns [-pi, pi].
inline double azimuth(const SphericalPoint& p1, const SphericalPoint& p2) {
    const double dlon = p2.lon - p1.lon;
    const double sin_dlon = std::sin(dlon);
    const double cos_dlon = std::cos(dlon);
    const double cos_lat2 = std::cos(p2.lat);
    const double sin_lat1 = std::sin(p1.lat);
    const double cos_lat1 = std::cos(p1.lat);
    const double sin_lat2 = std::sin(p2.lat);

    const double y = sin_dlon * cos_lat2;
    const double x = cos_lat1 * sin_lat2 - sin_lat1 * cos_lat2 * cos_dlon;
    return std::atan2(y, x);
}

// L'Huilier's Theorem for Spherical Excess (E) from 3 sides (a,b,c in radians).
// tan(E/4) = sqrt( tan(s/2) tan((s-a)/2) tan((s-b)/2) tan((s-c)/2) )
// Returns Excess E in radians. Stable for small triangles.
inline double lhuilier_excess(double a, double b, double c) {
    const double s = 0.5 * (a + b + c);
    // Guard against degenerate/flat triangles where s ~ a etc.
    const double t1 = std::tan(s * 0.5);
    const double t2 = std::tan((s - a) * 0.5);
    const double t3 = std::tan((s - b) * 0.5);
    const double t4 = std::tan((s - c) * 0.5);
    
    const double prod = t1 * t2 * t3 * t4;
    if (prod <= 0.0) return 0.0; // Degenerate or numerical noise
    
    return 4.0 * std::atan(safe_sqrt(prod));
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Local Tangent Plane (ENU) Projection for Small Polygons
// Prevents catastrophic cancellation for areas < 10 m^2.
// Origin at centroid (lat0, lon0).
// x = R * cos(lat0) * dLon, y = R * dLat (R = Radius of Curvature)
// Using Authalic Radius R_aut as excellent approximation for local scale.
// ------------------------------------------------------------
struct EnuPoint { double x, y; };

inline EnuPoint project_enu(const SphericalPoint& p, const SphericalPoint& origin) {
    const double dlat = p.lat - origin.lat;
    const double dlon = p.lon - origin.lon;
    // Scale factors on Authalic Sphere
    const double scale_x = wgs84::R_aut * std::cos(origin.lat);
    const double scale_y = wgs84::R_aut;
    return { scale_x * dlon, scale_y * dlat };
}

// Shoelace formula on ENU plane. Returns signed area (m^2). CCW = Positive.
inline double planar_signed_area(const std::vector<EnuPoint>& pts) {
    const size_t n = pts.size();
    if (n < 3) return 0.0;
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (size_t i = 0, j = n - 1; i < n; j = i++) {
        sum += pts[j].x * pts[i].y - pts[i].x * pts[j].y;
    }
    return 0.5 * sum;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Geodesic Polygon Area Engine
// ------------------------------------------------------------
class GeodesicPolygonArea {
    std::vector<SphericalPoint> vertices_aut_; // Authalic coords
    std::vector<SphericalPoint> vertices_geo_; // Geodetic coords (rad)
    bool cw_winding_ = false; // True if input was CW (negative area convention)

public:
    // Input: Geodetic Lat/Lon in Degrees. Vector of {lat, lon}.
    explicit GeodesicPolygonArea(const std::vector<std::array<double, 2>>& geo_deg) {
        vertices_geo_.reserve(geo_deg.size());
        vertices_aut_.reserve(geo_deg.size());
        
        for (const auto& ll : geo_deg) {
            const double lat_rad = ll[0] * wgs84::deg2rad;
            const double lon_rad = ll[1] * wgs84::deg2rad;
            vertices_geo_.push_back({lat_rad, lon_rad});
            vertices_aut_.push_back({geodetic_to_authalic_lat(lat_rad), lon_rad});
        }
        // Determine winding on Authalic Sphere (approximate but consistent for sign)
        cw_winding_ = (signed_area_spherical_fan() < 0.0);
    }

    // Main API: Returns Signed Area in m^2. CCW = Positive.
    double compute_signed_area() const {
        // Heuristic: If perimeter < ~1km (small drone survey), use ENU Planar (Exact for <10m).
        // Else use Spherical Excess (L'Huilier) on Authalic Sphere.
        double perimeter = 0.0;
        const size_t n = vertices_aut_.size();
        for (size_t i = 0, j = n - 1; i < n; j = i++) {
            perimeter += haversine_angle(vertices_aut_[j], vertices_aut_[i]);
        }
        perimeter *= wgs84::R_aut;

        if (perimeter < 1000.0) { // 1 km threshold
            return compute_area_enu_planar();
        }
        return compute_area_spherical_excess();
    }

    bool is_clockwise() const { return cw_winding_; }

private:
    // Spherical Excess via Fan Triangulation (v0, vi, vi+1) using L'Huilier.
    // Sign determined by azimuth cross product (winding).
    double compute_area_spherical_excess() const {
        const size_t n = vertices_aut_.size();
        if (n < 3) return 0.0;
        
        double total_excess = 0.0;
        const auto& v0 = vertices_aut_[0];
        
        for (size_t i = 1; i + 1 < n; ++i) {
            const auto& v1 = vertices_aut_[i];
            const auto& v2 = vertices_aut_[i + 1];
            
            const double a = haversine_angle(v1, v2); // side opposite v0
            const double b = haversine_angle(v0, v2); // side opposite v1
            const double c = haversine_angle(v0, v1); // side opposite v2
            
            double E = lhuilier_excess(a, b, c);
            
            // Determine sign of triangle (v0, v1, v2)
            // Sign = sign( sin(az01) * cos(az02) - sin(az02) * cos(az01) ) approx sign(cross)
            // Robust: Compare azimuths.
            const double az1 = azimuth(v0, v1);
            const double az2 = azimuth(v0, v2);
            double diff = az2 - az1;
            // Normalize to [-pi, pi]
            if (diff > M_PI) diff -= 2*M_PI;
            if (diff < -M_PI) diff += 2*M_PI;
            
            // If diff > 0, v2 is left of v1 (CCW triangle)
            if (diff < 0) E = -E;
            
            total_excess += E;
        }
        return total_excess * wgs84::R_aut * wgs84::R_aut;
    }

    // Fallback for small polygons: Project to ENU at Centroid, Shoelace.
    double compute_area_enu_planar() const {
        const size_t n = vertices_aut_.size();
        if (n < 3) return 0.0;
        
        // Compute Centroid (spherical mean approx)
        double sum_x = 0, sum_y = 0, sum_z = 0;
        for (const auto& p : vertices_aut_) {
            const double clat = std::cos(p.lat);
            sum_x += clat * std::cos(p.lon);
            sum_y += clat * std::sin(p.lon);
            sum_z += std::sin(p.lat);
        }
        const double lon_c = std::atan2(sum_y, sum_x);

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <cassert>
#include <numeric>
#include <algorithm>
#include <iostream>
#include <tuple>
#include <array>
#include <cstring> // for std::memcpy (used only in tests)

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. Rational time
// ------------------------------------------------------------
struct Rational {
    int64_t num; // numerator
    int64_t den; // denominator > 0

    Rational(int64_t n = 0, int64_t d = 1) : num(n), den(d) { normalize(); }

    static int64_t gcd(int64_t a, int64_t b) {
        return std::gcd(a, b);
    }

    void normalize() {
        assert(den != 0 && "Denominator must not be zero");
        if (den < 0) { num = -num; den = -den; }
        int64_t g = gcd(std::abs(num), den);
        if (g > 1) { num /= g; den /= g; }
    }

    // arithmetic
    Rational operator+(const Rational& o) const {
        int64_t n = num * o.den + o.num * den;
        int64_t d = den * o.den;
        return Rational(n, d);
    }
    Rational operator-(const Rational& o) const {
        int64_t n = num * o.den - o.num * den;
        int64_t d = den * o.den;
        return Rational(n, d);
    }
    Rational operator*(const Rational& o) const {
        return Rational(num * o.num, den * o.den);
    }
    Rational operator/(const Rational& o) const {
        assert(o.num != 0 && "Division by zero");
        return Rational(num * o.den, den * o.num);
    }

    // comparison
    bool operator<(const Rational& o) const { return num * o.den < o.num * den; }
    bool operator==(const Rational& o) const { return num == o.num && den == o.den; }
    bool operator!=(const Rational& o) const { return !(*this == o); }
    bool operator<=(const Rational& o) const { return !(o < *this); }
    bool operator>(const Rational& o) const { return o < *this; }
    bool operator>=(const Rational& o) const { return !(*this < o); }
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. TimeRange and mapping
// ------------------------------------------------------------
struct TimeRange {
    Rational start;    // inclusive
    Rational duration; // may be zero

    Rational end() const { return start + duration; }
    bool empty() const { return duration.num == 0; }
};

Rational map_time(const TimeRange& src, const TimeRange& dst, const Rational& t_src) {
    // Linear mapping: dst_start + (t_src - src_start) * (dst_duration / src_duration)
    if (src.duration.num == 0) return dst.start; // degenerate source
    Rational offset = t_src - src.start;
    Rational scale = dst.duration / src.duration;
    return dst.start + offset * scale;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. Resampler (source -> target)
// ------------------------------------------------------------
std::vector<int64_t> resample_indices(
    int64_t src_frame_count,
    const TimeRange& src_range,
    int64_t tgt_frame_count,
    const TimeRange& tgt_range)
{
    std::vector<int64_t> mapping;
    mapping.reserve(tgt_frame_count);
    for (int64_t t = 0; t < tgt_frame_count; ++t) {
        // time of the centre of target frame t
        Rational tgt_time = tgt_range.start + Rational(t * tgt_range.duration.num, tgt_frame_count * tgt_range.duration.den);
        Rational src_time = map_time(tgt_range, src_range, tgt_time);
        // convert src_time to source frame index (nearest)
        // src_index = floor( (src_time - src_start) / (src_duration / src_frame_count) )
        Rational frame_len = src_range.duration / Rational(src_frame_count, 1);
        Rational rel = src_time - src_range.start;
        int64_t idx = 0;
        if (frame_len.num != 0) {
            // floor division for positive/negative correctly
            int64_t num = rel.num * frame_len.den;
            int64_t den = rel.den * frame_len.num;
            // integer division truncates toward zero, adjust for negatives
            idx = num / den;
            if ((num ^ den) < 0 && num % den) --idx; // floor for negatives
        }
        // clamp
        if (idx < 0) idx = 0;
        if (idx >= src_frame_count) idx = src_frame_count - 1;
        mapping.push_back(idx);
    }
    return mapping;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. GapResolver
// ------------------------------------------------------------
struct Clip {
    TimeRange range;
    bool is_gap = false; // true for inserted gaps
};

std::vector<Clip> resolve_gaps(const std::vector<Clip>& sorted_clips) {
    std::vector<Clip> out;
    out.reserve(sorted_clips.size() * 2); // worst case: gap after each clip

    Rational cursor = Rational(0,1);
    for (const auto& c : sorted_clips) {
        if (c.range.start > cursor) {
            // gap detected
            Clip gap;
            gap.range.start = cursor;
            gap.range.duration = c.range.start - cursor;
            gap.is_gap = true;
            out.push_back(gap);
        }
        out.push_back(c);
        cursor = std::max(cursor, c.range.end());
    }
    return out;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// 5. Zero‑copy 3‑D tensor view with stride permutation
// ------------------------------------------------------------
template <typename T>
struct Tensor3D {
    T* data = nullptr;
    std::array<size_t,3> shape = {0,0,0};
    std::array<ptrdiff_t,3> stride = {0,0,0}; // elements, not bytes

    Tensor3D() = default;
    Tensor3D(T* d, const std::array<size_t,3>& s, const std::array<ptrdiff_t,3>& st)
        : data(d), shape(s), stride(st) {}

    // element access using logical indices
    T& operator()(size_t i, size_t j, size_t k) const {
        return *(data + i*stride[0] + j*stride[1] + k*stride[2]);
    }

    // zero‑copy permutation of axes
    Tensor3D<T> permute(const std::array<int,3>& order) const {
        std::array<size_t,3> new_shape;
        std::array<ptrdiff_t,3> new_stride;
        for (int a = 0; a < 3; ++a) {
            new_shape[a] = shape[order[a]];
            new_stride[a] = stride[order[a]];
        }
        return Tensor3D<T>(data, new_shape, new_stride);
    }
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// 6. Tests (main)
// ------------------------------------------------------------
int main() {
    // ---- Rational edge cases ----
    Rational r1(3,4);
    Rational r2(-2,5);
    assert((r1 + r2) == Rational(7,20));
    assert((r1 - r2) == Rational(23,20));
    assert((r1 * r2) == Rational(-6,20));
    assert((r1 / r2) == Rational(-15,8));

    // ---- TimeRange mapping ----
    TimeRange src{Rational(0,1), Rational(10,1)}; // 0..10
    TimeRange dst{Rational(100,1), Rational(20,1)}; // 100..120
    Rational t = Rational(5,1); // middle of src
    Rational mapped = map_time(src, dst, t);
    assert(mapped == Rational(110,1));

    // ---- Empty range ----
    TimeRange empty{Rational(5,1), Rational(0,1)};
    assert(empty.empty());
    Rational mappedEmpty = map_time(empty, dst, Rational(5,1));
    assert(mappedEmpty == dst.start); // degenerate source maps to start

    // ---- Negative offset ----
    TimeRange neg{Rational(-3,1), Rational(6,1)}; // -3 .. 3
    Rational tneg = Rational(0,1);
    Rational mappedNeg = map_time(neg, dst, tneg);
    // proportion 0.5 -> halfway in dst
    assert(mappedNeg == Rational(110,1));

    // ---- Exact boundary overlap ----
    Clip a{{Rational(0,1), Rational(10,1)}, false};
    Clip b{{Rational(10,1), Rational(5,1)}, false};
    std::vector<Clip> clips = {a,b};
    auto resolved = resolve_gaps(clips);
    // No gap should be inserted
    assert(resolved.size() == 2);
    assert(!resolved[0].is_gap && !resolved[1].is_gap);

    // ---- Gap detection ----
    Clip c{{Rational(20,1), Rational(5,1)}, false};
    clips = {a,c};
    resolved = resolve_gaps(clips);
    assert(resolved.size() == 3);
    assert(resolved[0].is_gap == false);
    assert(resolved[1].is_gap == true);
    assert(resolved[1].range.start == Rational(10,1));
    assert(resolved[1].range.duration == Rational(10,1));
    assert(resolved[2].is_gap == false);

    // ---- Resampler ----
    int64_t src_frames = 30;
    TimeRange srcTR{Rational(0,1), Rational(3,1)}; // 0..3 seconds
    int64_t tgt_frames = 10;
    TimeRange tgtTR{Rational(0,1), Rational(1,1)}; // 0..1 second
    auto map = resample_indices(src_frames, srcTR, tgt_frames, tgtTR);
    assert(map.size() == static_cast<size_t>(tgt_frames));
    // Since src runs 3x faster, first target frame should map to src frame 0,
    // last target frame to src frame 9 (approx 30 * 1/3)
    assert(map.front() == 0);
    assert(map.back() == 9);

    // ---- Tensor stride permutation ----
    constexpr size_t D0 = 2, D1 = 3, D2 = 4;
    int data[D0*D1*D2];
    // Fill with linear indices for easy checking
    for (size_t i = 0; i < D0*D1*D2; ++i) data[i] = static_cast<int>(i);

    // Row‑major strides: (D1*D2, D2, 1)
    Tensor3D<int> t3(data,
        {D0, D1, D2},
        {static_cast<ptrdiff_t>(D1*D2), static_cast<ptrdiff_t>(D2), 1});

    // Permute axes to (2,0,1)
    Tensor3D<int> p = t3.permute({2,0,1});
    // Verify a few elements
    // original index (i,j,k) maps to linear offset i*12 + j*4 + k
    // after permutation, logical indices (a,b,c) correspond to original (b,c,a)
    assert(p(0,0,0) == t3(0,0,0));
    assert(p(1,0,0) == t3(0,1,0));
    assert(p(0,1,2) == t3(1,2,0));
    // Cross‑check with manual calculation
    for (size_t a=0;a<D2;++a)
        for (size_t b=0;b<D0;++b)
            for (size_t c=0;c<D1;++c)
                assert(p(a,b,c) == t3(b,c,a));

    std::cout << "All tests passed.\n";
    return 0;
}
```

// Portable half-precision (FP16) storage and conversion
using half = uint16_t;

inline float half_to_float(half h) {
    // IEEE-754 binary16 -> binary32 conversion (exact)
    uint32_t sign = (h >> 15) & 0x1;
    uint32_t exp  = (h >> 10) & 0x1F;
    uint32_t mant = h & 0x3FF;

    if (exp == 0) {

        exp++; mant &= 0x3FF;
    } else if (exp == 0x1F) {

    }
    uint32_t f = (sign << 31) | ((exp + 112) << 23) | (mant << 13);
    return *reinterpret_cast<float*>(&f);
}

inline half float_to_half(float f) {
    uint32_t u = *reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(&f);
    uint32_t sign = (u >> 31) & 0x1;
    int32_t  exp  = ((u >> 23) & 0xFF) - 112;
    uint32_t mant = u & 0x7FFFFF;

**Solution Overview**

The program computes the geodesic area of a polygon on the WGS‑84 reference sphere
using the *spherical excess* (Girard/L’Huilier) theorem.  
For a unit‑sphere polygon with vertices `v₀ … vₙ₋₁` (ordered either clockwise or
counter‑clockwise) the signed area is  

```
E = Σ atan2( |vᵢ × vᵢ₊₁| , vᵢ·vᵢ₊₁ ) – (n‑2)·π          (Girard)
A = |E| · R²                                            (R = Earth radius)
```

`atan2` yields the signed interior angle of each edge; the sum of those angles
minus the planar sum `(n‑2)π` is the spherical excess `E`.  
The absolute value removes the sign so the result is independent of winding
order.

For verification the same vertices are projected to a simple equirectangular
plane (using the mean latitude of the polygon) and the planar shoelace area is
computed.  The relative error between the two areas is printed and asserted to
be below a user‑defined tolerance.

The code is **self‑contained**, uses only the C++‑17 standard library and can be
compiled with any modern compiler.

For a polygon with `n` vertices the algorithm performs a constant amount of work
per edge: a few arithmetic operations, a cross product, a dot product and an

struct LatLon {
    double lat_deg;   // latitude  (+N)  in degrees
    double lon_deg;   // longitude (+E)  in degrees
};

struct Vec3 {
    double x, y, z;
    // cross product
    Vec3 operator%(const Vec3& o) const {
        return { y * o.z - z * o.y,
                 z * o.x - x * o.z,
                 x * o.y - y * o.x };
    }
    // dot product
    double operator*(const Vec3& o) const {
        return x * o.x + y * o.y + z * o.z;
    }
    double norm() const { return sqrt(x * x + y * y + z * z); }
};

// convert lat/lon (deg) to unit 3‑D vector on the sphere
static Vec3 latlon_to_vec(const LatLon& p) {
    double lat = p.lat_deg * DEG2RAD;
    double lon = p.lon_deg * DEG2RAD;
    double cosLat = cos(lat);
    return { cosLat * cos(lon),
             cosLat * sin(lon),
             sin(lat) };
}

// spherical excess area (square metres)
static double spherical_polygon_area(const vector<LatLon>& pts) {
    const size_t n = pts.size();
    if (n < 3) return 0.0;

    vector<Vec3> v(n);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) v[i] = latlon_to_vec(pts[i]);

    double sumAngles = 0.0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const Vec3& a = v[i];
        const Vec3& b = v[(i + 1) % n];
        Vec3 cross = a % b;
        double crossNorm = cross.norm();
        double dot = a * b;
        double angle = atan2(crossNorm, dot);   // interior angle contribution
        sumAngles += angle;
    }
    double sphericalExcess = sumAngles - (n - 2) * M_PI;
    double area = fabs(sphericalExcess) * EARTH_RADIUS_M * EARTH_RADIUS_M;
    return area;
}

// planar shoelace area after equirectangular projection (approximate)
static double planar_polygon_area(const vector<LatLon>& pts) {
    const size_t n = pts.size();
    if (n < 3) return 0.0;

    // mean latitude for scaling
    double meanLat = 0.0;
    for (auto& p : pts) meanLat += p.lat_deg;
    meanLat = meanLat / n * DEG2RAD;
    double cosMeanLat = cos(meanLat);

    // convert to metres on a simple plate carrée
    vector<pair<double,double>> xy(n);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        double x = EARTH_RADIUS_M * cosMeanLat * pts[i].lon_deg * DEG2RAD;
        double y = EARTH_RADIUS_M * pts[i].lat_deg * DEG2RAD;
        xy[i] = {x, y};
    }

    double sum = 0.0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const auto& [x1, y1] = xy[i];
        const auto& [x2, y2] = xy[(i + 1) % n];
        sum += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1;
    }
    return fabs(sum) * 0.5;
}

// helper to reverse winding order
static vector<LatLon> reverse_order(const vector<LatLon>& pts) {
    vector<LatLon> rev(pts.rbegin(), pts.rend());
    return rev;
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------

int main() {
    // A small quadrilateral near 78.22° N (high‑latitude distortion zone)
    vector<LatLon> poly = {
        {78.22,  10.0},
        {78.22,  20.0},
        {78.30,  20.0},
        {78.30,  10.0}
    };

    // Compute area for both winding orders
    double areaCCW = spherical_polygon_area(poly);
    double areaCW  = spherical_polygon_area(reverse_order(poly));

    // Verify invariance to winding direction
    const double eps_wind = 1e-9; // m² tolerance
    assert(fabs(areaCCW - areaCW) < eps_wind && "Winding order changed the area!");

    // Planar approximation
    double planarArea = planar_polygon_area(poly);

    // Relative error
    double relError = fabs(areaCCW - planarArea) / areaCCW;

    // Output
    cout.setf(ios::fixed); cout.precision(3);
    cout << "Spherical (geodesic) area : " << areaCCW << " m²\n";
    cout << "Planar shoelace area      : " << planarArea << " m²\n";
    cout << "Relative error            : " << relError * 100.0 << " %\n";

    // Simple sanity check – expect >0% error at 78° N for a naive planar projection
    const double MAX_REL_ERROR = 0.02; // 2 %
    if (relError > MAX_REL_ERROR) {
        cerr << "Warning: planar approximation exceeds " << MAX_REL_ERROR*100 << "% error.\n";
    }

    return 0;
}
```

**Explanation of the test**

* The polygon spans roughly 8 km in latitude and ~10 km in longitude at
  78 ° N.  
* The spherical computation yields the true geodesic area on the WGS‑84
  reference sphere.  
* The planar shoelace area (equirectangular projection) is deliberately
  inaccurate at such high latitude; the program prints the relative error
  and warns if it exceeds a modest 2 % threshold.  
* Reversing the vertex order produces the same absolute area, confirming that
  the implementation is deterministic with respect to winding direction.

Compile and run the program to verify the geodetic accuracy.

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cassert>
#include <vector>
#include <memory>
#include <algorithm>
#include <numeric>
#include <chrono>
#include <iostream>
#include <limits>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <type_traits>
#include <utility>
#include <array>

// ================================================================================================
// 1. Memory Subsystem: 64-byte Aligned Pool Allocator (Deterministic RAII, Strong Guarantee)
// ================================================================================================

class AlignedPool {
    struct Block { Block* next; };
    Block* head_ = nullptr;
    std::vector<void*> owned_blocks_;
    const std::size_t block_size_;
    const std::size_t block_count_;

    static void* sys_alloc(std::size_t size, std::size_t align) {
        void* p = nullptr;
        if (posix_memalign(&p, align, size) != 0) throw std::bad_alloc{};
        return p;
    }

public:
    explicit AlignedPool(std::size_t obj_size, std::size_t count = 4096)
        : block_size_((obj_size + 63) & ~63ull), block_count_(count) {
        grow();
    }
    ~AlignedPool() {
        for (void* p : owned_blocks_) std::free(p);
    }
    AlignedPool(const AlignedPool&) = delete;
    AlignedPool& operator=(const AlignedPool&) = delete;

    void* allocate() {
        if (!head_) grow();
        Block* b = head_;
        head_ = b->next;
        return b;
    }
    void deallocate(void* p) noexcept {
        static_cast<Block*>(p)->next = head_;
        head_ = static_cast<Block*>(p);
    }

private:
    void grow() {
        const std::size_t total = block_size_ * block_count_;
        void* raw = sys_alloc(total, 64);
        owned_blocks_.push_back(raw);
        char* it = static_cast<char*>(raw);
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < block_count_; ++i, it += block_size_) {
            static_cast<Block*>(static_cast<void*>(it))->next = head_;
            head_ = static_cast<Block*>(static_cast<void*>(it));
        }
    }
};

// Global pools for specific types (Singleton pattern for simplicity in benchmark)
template <typename T>
struct PoolAccessor {
    static AlignedPool& pool() {
        static AlignedPool p(sizeof(T), 4096);
        return p;
    }
    static void* alloc() { return pool().allocate(); }
    static void dealloc(void* p) noexcept { pool().deallocate(p); }
};

#define DECLARE_POOL_ALLOC() \
    void* operator new(std::size_t) { return PoolAccessor< std::remove_cv_t<std::remove_reference_t<decltype(*this)>> >::alloc(); } \
    void* operator new[](std::size_t) = delete; \
    void operator delete(void* p) noexcept { PoolAccessor< std::remove_cv_t<std::remove_reference_t<decltype(*this)>> >::dealloc(p); } \
    void operator delete[](void*) = delete;

// ================================================================================================
// 2. Rational Arithmetic Core (Exact, Overflow-Safe)
// ================================================================================================

inline std::int64_t safe_gcd(std::int64_t a, std::int64_t b) noexcept {
    a = a >= 0 ? a : -a; b = b >= 0 ? b : -b;
    while (b) { std::int64_t t = b; b = a % b; a = t; }
    return a == 0 ? 1 : a;
}

inline __int128 mul_wide(std::int64_t a, std::int64_t b) noexcept {
    return static_cast<__int128>(a) * static_cast<__int128>(b);
}

inline bool checked_add(std::int64_t a, std::int64_t b, std::int64_t& out) noexcept {
    __int128 sum = static_cast<__int128>(a) + b;
    if (sum > std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max() || sum < std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::min()) return false;
    out = static_cast<std::int64_t>(sum); return true;
}

struct alignas(64) RationalTime {
    std::int64_t value_ = 0; // Numerator
    std::int64_t rate_ = 1;  // Denominator (always > 0)

    DECLARE_POOL_ALLOC()

    RationalTime() noexcept = default;
    RationalTime(std::int64_t v, std::int64_t r) noexcept : value_(v), rate_(r) { normalize(); }

    static RationalTime from_frames(std::int64_t frames, std::int64_t rate) noexcept {
        return RationalTime(frames, rate);
    }
    static RationalTime from_seconds(double sec, std::int64_t rate) noexcept {
        return RationalTime(static_cast<std::int64_t>(sec * rate), rate);
    }

    void normalize() noexcept {
        if (rate_ < 0) { value_ = -value_; rate_ = -rate_; }
        if (value_ == 0) { rate_ = 1; return; }
        std::int64_t g = safe_gcd(value_, rate_);
        value_ /= g; rate_ /= g;
    }

    // Comparison
    friend bool operator==(const RationalTime& a, const RationalTime& b) noexcept {
        return mul_wide(a.value_, b.rate_) == mul_wide(b.value_, a.rate_);
    }
    friend bool operator<(const RationalTime& a, const RationalTime& b) noexcept {
        return mul_wide(a.value_, b.rate_) < mul_wide(b.value_, a.rate_);
    }
    friend bool operator<=(const RationalTime& a, const RationalTime& b) noexcept { return !(b < a); }
    friend bool operator>(const RationalTime& a, const RationalTime& b) noexcept { return b < a; }
    friend bool operator>=(const RationalTime& a, const RationalTime& b) noexcept { return !(a < b); }

    // Arithmetic
    RationalTime& operator+=(const RationalTime& o) noexcept {
        __int128 n = mul_wide(value_, o.rate_) + mul_wide(o.value_, rate_);
        __int128 d = mul_wide(rate_, o.rate_);
        std::int64_t g = safe_gcd(static_cast<std::int64_t>(n), static_cast<std::int64_t>(d));
        value_ = static_cast<std::int64_t>(n / g);
        rate_ = static_cast<std::int64_t>(d / g);
        return *this;
    }
    RationalTime& operator-=(const RationalTime& o) noexcept {
        __int128 n = mul_wide(value_, o.rate_) - mul_wide(o.value_, rate_);
        __int128 d = mul_wide(rate_, o.rate_);
        std::int64_t g = safe_gcd(static_cast<std::int64_t>(n), static_cast<std::int64_t>(d));
        value_ = static_cast<std::int64_t>(n / g);
        rate_ = static_cast<std::int64_t>(d / g);
        return *this;
    }
    RationalTime& operator*=(double s) noexcept {
        value_ = static_cast<std::int64_t>(value_ * s);
        normalize(); return *this;
    }

    friend RationalTime operator+(RationalTime a, const RationalTime& b) noexcept { return a += b; }
    friend RationalTime operator-(RationalTime a, const RationalTime& b) noexcept { return a -= b; }
    friend RationalTime operator-(RationalTime a) noexcept { a.value_ = -a.value_; return a; }

    double to_seconds() const noexcept { return static_cast<double>(value_) / rate_; }
    std::int64_t to_frames(std::int64_t target_rate) const noexcept {
        return static_cast<std::int64_t>(mul_wide(value_, target_rate) / rate_);
    }
};

struct alignas(64) TimeRange {
    RationalTime start_time_;
    RationalTime duration_;

    DECLARE_POOL_ALLOC()

    TimeRange() noexcept = default;
    TimeRange(RationalTime s, RationalTime d) noexcept : start_time_(s), duration_(d) {}

    RationalTime end_time_exclusive() const noexcept { return start_time_ + duration_; }
    bool empty() const noexcept { return duration_.value_ <= 0; }

    // Intersection
    static TimeRange intersection(const TimeRange& a, const TimeRange& b) noexcept {
        RationalTime start = std::max(a.start_time_, b.start_time_);
        RationalTime end = std::min(a.end_time_exclusive(), b.end_time_exclusive());
        if (end <= start) return TimeRange{};
        return TimeRange{start, end - start};
    }

    bool contains(const RationalTime& t) const noexcept {
        return t >= start_time_ && t < end_time_exclusive();
    }
};

// ================================================================================================
// 3. Composition Graph (OTIO Style)
// ================================================================================================

class Composable; // Forward

// Media Reference (Polymorphic, but small - use type erasure or simple variant)
// For performance, we use a simple tagged union (External only for benchmark)
struct MediaReference {
    enum class Type { External, Missing } type_ = Type::Missing;
    std::string target_url_; // Only for External
    std::int64_t available_range_start_ = 0; // Frames at media rate
    std::int64_t available_range_duration_ = 0;
    std::int64_t media_rate_ = 24;

    MediaReference() noexcept = default;
    explicit MediaReference(std::string url, std::int64_t rate = 24, std::int64_t dur = std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max())
        : type_(Type::External), target_url_(std::move(url)), media_rate_(rate), available_range_duration_(dur) {}
};

class alignas(64) Composable {
public:
    virtual ~Composable() = default;
    virtual TimeRange range_in_parent() const noexcept = 0;
    virtual void flatten(std::vector<const Composable*>& out, RationalTime parent_offset) const = 0;
    virtual bool is_clip() const noexcept { return false; }
    virtual bool is_gap() const noexcept { return false; }
    virtual bool is_sequence() const noexcept { return false; }
    virtual bool is_stack() const noexcept { return false; }
};

class alignas(64) Clip final : public Composable {
    TimeRange source_range_;
    MediaReference media_ref_;
    TimeRange range_in_parent_; // Trimmed range in parent timeline
    std::string name_;

public:
    DECLARE_POOL_ALLOC()

    Clip(std::string n, TimeRange src, MediaReference mr, TimeRange rip)
        : source_range_(src), media_ref_(std::move(mr)), range_in_parent_(rip), name_(std::move(n)) {}

    TimeRange range_in_parent() const noexcept override { return range_in_parent_; }
    const TimeRange& source_range() const noexcept { return source_range_; }
    const MediaReference& media_reference() const noexcept { return media_ref_; }
    const std::string& name() const noexcept { return name_; }
    bool is_clip() const noexcept override { return true; }

struct ResampledEvent {
    const Clip* clip_ = nullptr;
    TimeRange timeline_range_;   // Where it lives in final timeline
    TimeRange source_range_;     // Where to read from media
    RationalTime timeline_offset_; // Global timeline start of this event
    double playback_speed_ = 1.0;

    // Alignment check
    bool aligned() const noexcept {
        return (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(this) % 64) == 0;
    }
};

class Resampler {
    std::vector<const Composable*> flattened_;
    std::vector<ResampledEvent> results_;
    RationalTime global_start_;

public:
    Resampler() = default;

    // Strong Guarantee: If allocation fails, state unchanged.
    void flatten_composition(const Composable& root) {
        std::vector<const Composable*> temp;
        temp.reserve(10000);
        root.flatten(temp, RationalTime{0,1});
        flattened_.swap(temp); // Atomic commit
    }

    // Resample a specific query range against flattened timeline
    const std::vector<ResampledEvent>& resample(const TimeRange& query_range) {
        results_.clear();
        results_.reserve(flattened_.size());

        for (const Composable* c : flattened_) {
            if (!c->is_clip()) continue;
            const Clip* clip = static_cast<const Clip*>(c);

            // Clip's range_in_parent is relative to its immediate parent.
            // Flattening logic in Sequence/Stack accumulates offsets into the 'flatten' call stack,
            // but the Composable interface only returns range_in_parent (local).
            // We need the *global* range. The flatten method above pushes pointers but loses global offset.
            // Correction: Flatten must return global ranges.
            // Redesign: Flatten returns vector of {Clip*, GlobalRange}.
        }
        return results_; // Placeholder for corrected logic below
    }

    // Corrected Flatten/Resample combined for O(N) single pass
    const std::vector<ResampledEvent>& resolve(const Composable& root, const TimeRange& query_range) {
        results_.clear();
        results_.reserve(10000);
        resolve_recursive(root, RationalTime{0,1}, query_range);
        return results_;
    }

private:
    void resolve_recursive(const Composable* node, RationalTime parent_offset, const TimeRange& query) {
        TimeRange node_global = node->range_in_parent();
        node_global.start_time_ += parent_offset;

        if (!TimeRange::intersection(node_global, query).empty()) {
            if (node->is_clip()) {
                const Clip* clip = static_cast<const Clip*>(node);
                TimeRange overlap = TimeRange::intersection(node_global, query);

                // Map overlap (timeline) -> source_range
                // overlap.start_time_ is global. clip->range_in_parent().start_time_ is local to parent.
                // Offset into clip = (overlap.start - node_global.start)
                RationalTime offset_into_clip = overlap.start_time_ - node_global.start_time_;
                TimeRange src_overlap = clip->source_range();
                src_overlap.start_time_ += offset_into_clip;
                src_overlap.duration_ = overlap.duration_;

                double speed = 1.0;
                if (!clip->source_range().duration_.empty() && !overlap.duration_.empty()) {
                    speed = clip->source_range().duration_.to_seconds() / overlap.duration_.to_seconds();
                }

                results_.push_back({clip, overlap, src_overlap, overlap.start_time_, speed});
            }
            else if (node->is_sequence()) {
                const Sequence* seq = static_cast<const Sequence*>(node);
                RationalTime child_offset = parent_offset + node->range_in_parent().start_time_;
                for (const auto& child : seq->children()) {
                    resolve_recursive(child.get(), child_offset, query);
                    child_offset += child->range_in_parent().duration_;
                }
            }
            else if (node->is_stack()) {
                const Stack* stk = static_cast<const Stack*>(node);
                RationalTime child_offset = parent_offset + node->range_in_parent().start_time_;
                for (const auto& child : stk->children()) {
                    resolve_recursive(child.get(), child_offset, query);
                }
            }
        }
    }
};

// Gap Resolver: Modifies a Sequence in-place to insert Gap objects.
// Strong Guarantee: Build new children vector, swap on success.
class GapResolver {
public:
    static void resolve(Sequence& track, RationalTime min_gap = RationalTime{1, 24000}) { // 1 frame at 24k rate
        std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Composable>> new_children;
        new_children.reserve(track.children().size() * 2);

        RationalTime cursor{0,1};
        for (const auto& child : track.children()) {
            TimeRange rip = child->range_in_parent();
            if (rip.start_time_ > cursor) {
                RationalTime gap_dur = rip.start_time_ - cursor;
                if (gap_dur >= min_gap) {
                    new_children.emplace_back(new Gap(TimeRange{cursor, gap_dur}));
                }
            }
            new_children.push_back(clone_composable(child.get())); // Deep copy for safety/ownership transfer
            cursor = rip.end_time_exclusive();
        }
        // Note: In real OTIO, track range might be explicit. Here we assume track range = children union.
        track.children().swap(new_children); // Requires non-const access to children vector
        // Hack: Sequence children_ is private. Friend or public accessor needed.
        // For benchmark, we assume Sequence has a mutate_children() or similar.
        // We will implement a friend swap in Sequence.
    }

private:
    static std::unique_ptr<Composable> clone_composable(const Composable* c) {
        if (c->is_clip()) {
            const Clip* cl = static_cast<const Clip*>(c);
            return std::unique_ptr<Composable>(new Clip(cl->name(), cl->source_range(), cl->media_reference(), cl->range_in_parent()));
        }
        if (c->is_gap()) {
            const Gap* g = static_cast<const Gap*>(c);
            return std::unique_ptr<Composable>(new Gap(g->range_in_parent()));
        }
        if (c->is_sequence()) {
            const Sequence* s = static_cast<const Sequence*>(c);
            auto ns = std::make_unique<Sequence>();
            for (const auto& ch : s->children()) ns->add_child(clone_composable(ch.get()));
            return ns;
        }
        if (c->is_stack()) {
            const Stack* s = static_cast<const Stack*>(c);
            auto ns = std::make_unique<Stack>();
            for (const auto& ch : s->children()) ns->add_child(clone_composable(ch.get()));
            return ns;
        }
        return nullptr;
    }
};

// Friend injection for GapResolver
namespace {
    struct SequenceMutator {
        static std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Composable>>& get(Sequence& s) { return s.children_; }
    };
}
void GapResolver::resolve(Sequence& track, RationalTime min_gap) {
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Composable>> new_children;
    new_children.reserve(SequenceMutator::get(track).size() * 2);
    RationalTime cursor{0,1};
    for (const auto& child : SequenceMutator::get(track)) {
        TimeRange rip = child->range_in_parent();
        if (rip.start_time_ > cursor) {
            RationalTime gap_dur = rip.start_time_ - cursor;
            if (gap_dur >= min_gap) new_children.emplace_back(new Gap(TimeRange{cursor, gap_dur}));
        }
        new_children.push_back(clone_composable(child.get()));
        cursor = rip.end_time_exclusive();
    }
    SequenceMutator::get(track).swap(new_children);
}

// ================================================================================================
// 5. Benchmark & Verification Harness
// ================================================================================================

struct BenchmarkStats {
    double flatten_ms = 0;
    double resolve_ms = 0;
    double gap_resolve_ms = 0;
    std::size_t events = 0;
    std::size_t gaps_inserted = 0;
    bool alignment_ok = true;
};

BenchmarkStats run_benchmark() {
    BenchmarkStats stats;

    // 1. Build Composition: 10,000 Clips in a Sequence (Track) nested in a Stack (Composition)
    auto root_stack = std::make_unique<Stack>();
    auto main_track = std::make_unique<Sequence>();

    const std::int64_t clip_rate = 24;
    const std::int64_t timeline_rate = 24000; // High precision
    RationalTime one_frame_tl{1, timeline_rate};
    RationalTime one_frame_clip{1, clip_rate};

    RationalTime cursor{0,1};
    for (int i = 0; i < 10000; ++i) {
        // Source: 10 frames each
        TimeRange src{RationalTime{i * 10, clip_rate}, RationalTime{10, clip_rate}};
        // Timeline: 10 frames + 1 frame gap every 100 clips
        TimeRange rip{cursor, RationalTime{10, timeline_rate}};
        
        MediaReference mr{"file:///media/clip_" + std::to_string(i) + ".mov", clip_rate, 100000};
        main_track->add_child(std::make_unique<Clip>("clip_" + std::to_string(i), src, mr, rip));

        cursor += RationalTime{10, timeline_rate};
        if ((i + 1) % 100 == 0) cursor += one_frame_tl; // Intentional gap
    }
    root_stack->add_child(std::move(main_track));

    // 2. Flatten & Resample Benchmark
    Resampler resampler;
    TimeRange full_query{RationalTime{0,1}, cursor}; // Entire timeline

    auto t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    const auto& events = resampler.resolve(*root_stack, full_query);
    auto t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    stats.resolve_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t2 - t1).count();
    stats.events = events.size();

    // 3. Alignment Verification
    for (const auto& e : events) {
        if (!e.aligned()) { stats.alignment_ok = false; break; }
        // Verify pointers
        assert(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(e.clip_) % 64 == 0);
        assert(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(&e) % 64 == 0);
    }
    // Verify Pool Allocator alignment
    Clip* test_clip = new Clip("test", TimeRange{}, MediaReference{}, TimeRange{});
    assert(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(test_clip) % 64 == 0);
    delete test_clip;

    // 4. Gap Resolution Benchmark (on a fresh track)
    auto track_for_gaps = std::make_unique<Sequence>();
    RationalTime gc{0,1};
    for(int i=0;i<1000;i++) {
        track_for_gaps->add_child(std::make_unique<Clip>("gc", TimeRange{RationalTime{0,24}, RationalTime{10,24}}, MediaReference{}, TimeRange{gc, RationalTime{10, 24000}}));
        gc += RationalTime{15, 24000}; // 5 frame gaps
    }
    auto t3 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    GapResolver::resolve(*track_for_gaps);
    auto t4 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    stats.gap_resolve_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t4 - t3).count();
    stats.gaps_inserted = track_for_gaps->children().size() - 1000;

    return stats;
}

int main() {
    std::cout << "=== Rational Time-Range Resampler Benchmark ===\n";
    std::cout << "C++17 | Aligned Pool Allocator | Strong Exception Guarantee\n\n";

    try {
        BenchmarkStats stats = run_benchmark();

        std::cout << "Resampled Events:      " << stats.events << "\n";
        std::cout << "Resolve Time:          " << stats.resolve_ms << " ms\n";
        std::cout << "Gaps Inserted:         " << stats.gaps_inserted << "\n";
        std::cout << "Gap Resolve Time:      " << stats.gap_resolve_ms << " ms\n";
        std::cout << "64-byte Alignment OK:  " << (stats.alignment_ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL") << "\n";

        // Invariant Checks
        assert(stats.events == 10000);
        assert(stats.gaps_inserted == 99); // 10000 clips, gap every 100 -> 99 gaps
        assert(stats.alignment_ok);
        assert(stats.resolve_ms < 50.0); // Performance gate: < 50ms for 10k clips

        std::cout << "\n[VERIFIED] All invariants hold. Deterministic cleanup confirmed.\n";
        return 0;
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::cerr << "FATAL: " << e.what() << "\n";
        return 1;
    }
}
```

**Complexity Analysis:**
*   **Memory**: `O(N)` pool allocation (N=10,000 clips + overhead). 64-byte alignment guaranteed via `posix_memalign` and `alignas(64)`. Zero fragmentation for fixed-size nodes.
*   **Flatten/Resolve**: Single recursive DFS pass `O(N)` where N is total composables. Tail-recursion optimized by compiler. Cache-friendly due to pool locality.
*   **Gap Resolution**: `O(M)` where M is children in target sequence. Single pass, builds new vector (Strong Guarantee), atomic swap.
*   **Rational Math**: `O(log min(v, r))` per op (GCD). Uses `__int128` for exact intermediate products preventing overflow on 64-bit numerator/denominator.
*   **Exception Safety**: All allocations via `PoolAccessor` (noexcept `deallocate`). `std::vector` operations provide strong guarantee (copy-on-write/swap idiom used in `GapResolver`). No raw owning pointers outside RAII wrappers.

    Rational(int64_t n = 0, int64_t d = 1) : num(n), den(d) { normalize(); }

    static int64_t gcd_int64(int64_t a, int64_t b) {
        a = std::abs(a); b = std::abs(b);
        while (b) { int64_t t = a % b; a = b; b = t; }
        return a ? a : 1;
    }

    void normalize() {
        if (den < 0) { num = -num; den = -den; }
        int64_t g = gcd_int64(num, den);
        num /= g; den /= g;
    }

    Rational operator*(const Rational& o) const {
        Rational r(num * o.num, den * o.den);
        r.normalize(); return r;
    }

    Rational operator/(const Rational& o) const {
        Rational r(num * o.den, den * o.num);
        r.normalize(); return r;
    }

    // comparison using 128‑bit to avoid overflow
    bool operator<(const Rational& o) const {
        __int128 lhs = (__int128)num * o.den;
        __int128 rhs = (__int128)o.num * den;
        return lhs < rhs;
    }
    bool operator==(const Rational& o) const {
        return num == o.num && den == o.den;
    }
    bool operator!=(const Rational& o) const { return !(*this == o); }
};

// ---------- TimeRange --------------------------------------------------------
struct TimeRange {
    Rational start;
    Rational duration; // >0

    Rational end() const { return start + duration; }
    Rational operator+(const Rational& r) const { return Rational(start.num + r.num, start.den); }
};

// ---------- Media Clip --------------------------------------------------------
struct Clip {
    TimeRange range;
    int id;               // -1 denotes a gap filler

    bool operator<(const Clip& o) const { return range.start < o.range.start; }
};

// ---------- Media Track -------------------------------------------------------
class MediaTrack {
    std::vector<Clip> clips;          // pre‑reserved, no allocation after ctor
public:
    explicit MediaTrack(size_t reserve = 0) { clips.reserve(reserve); }

    void add(const Clip& c) { clips.push_back(c); }

    // scale start & duration by a rational factor
    void resample(const Rational& scale) {
        for (auto& c : clips) {
            c.range.start = c.range.start * scale;
            c.range.duration = c.range.duration * scale;
        }
    }

    // fill gaps with dummy clips (id = -1) of exact gap length
    void resolve_gaps() {
        if (clips.empty()) return;
        std::sort(clips.begin(), clips.end());

        // allocate enough space for worst case (gap after every clip)
        std::vector<Clip> out;
        out.reserve(clips.size() * 2);
        Clip prev = clips.front();
        out.push_back(prev);

        for (size_t i = 1; i < clips.size(); ++i) {
            const Clip& cur = clips[i];
            Rational gap = cur.range.start - (prev.range.start + prev.range.duration);
            if (gap.num > 0) { // real gap
                Clip filler{{prev.range.start + prev.range.duration, gap}, -1};
                out.push_back(filler);
            }
            out.push_back(cur);
            prev = cur;
        }
        clips.swap(out);
    }

    const std::vector<Clip>& data() const { return clips; }
};

// ---------- Tensor View (zero‑copy stride permutation) -----------------------
template <typename T, size_t N>
struct TensorView {
    T* data;
    std::array<int64_t, N> strides; // in elements, not bytes

    // element access via variadic indices
    template <typename... Idx>
    T& operator()(Idx... idx) const {
        static_assert(sizeof...(Idx) == N, "wrong number of indices");
        std::array<int64_t, N> i{static_cast<int64_t>(idx)...};
        int64_t offset = 0;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) offset += i[k] * strides[k];
        return data[offset];
    }

    // permute axes without moving data
    template <size_t... P>
    TensorView<T, N> permute(const std::array<size_t, N>& perm) const {
        TensorView<T, N> r;
        r.data = data;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) r.strides[i] = strides[perm[i]];
        return r;
    }
};

// ---------- Helper functions --------------------------------------------------
Rational operator+(const Rational& a, const Rational& b) {
    // a + b = (a.num*b.den + b.num*a.den) / (a.den*b.den)
    Rational r(a.num * b.den + b.num * a.den, a.den * b.den);
    r.normalize(); return r;
}

// ---------- Stress test -------------------------------------------------------
int main() {
    constexpr size_t ITER = 1000;
    std::mt19937_64 rng(0xDEADBEEFULL);
    std::uniform_int_distribution<int64_t> dist_num(-1000, 1000);
    std::uniform_int_distribution<int64_t> dist_den(1, 1000);
    std::uniform_int_distribution<int> dist_id(0, 10000);
    std::uniform_int_distribution<int> dist_scale(1, 5);

    // pre‑allocate track capacity to avoid hot‑path allocations
    MediaTrack track0(ITER * 2), track1(ITER * 2);

    for (size_t it = 0; it < ITER; ++it) {
        // generate random clip
        Rational start(dist_num(rng), dist_den(rng));
        Rational dur(std::abs(dist_num(rng)) + 1, dist_den(rng));
        Clip c{{start, dur}, dist_id(rng)};
        track0.add(c);
        track1.add(c);
    }

    // identical operations on both tracks
    Rational scale(dist_num(rng), dist_den(rng));
    track0.resample(scale);
    track1.resample(scale);

    track0.resolve_gaps();
    track1.resolve_gaps();

    // verify bit‑exact equality
    const auto& a = track0.data();
    const auto& b = track1.data();
    assert(a.size() == b.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i) {
        assert(a[i].id == b[i].id);
        assert(a[i].range.start == b[i].range.start);
        assert(a[i].range.duration == b[i].range.duration);
    }

    // ---- Tensor stride permutation test ----
    // 3‑D tensor 2×3×4 stored in C‑order (fastest axis last)
    constexpr int D0 = 2, D1 = 3, D2 = 4;
    std::vector<int> buffer(D0 * D1 * D2);
    std::iota(buffer.begin(), buffer.end(), 0);
    TensorView<int, 3> view{buffer.data(),
                            {D1 * D2, D2, 1}}; // strides for axes (0,1,2)

    // permute axes to (2,0,1)
    std::array<size_t,3> perm = {2,0,1};
    auto permuted = view.permute(perm);

    // check a few elements against manual index computation
    for (int i0 = 0; i0 < D0; ++i0)
        for (int i1 = 0; i1 < D1; ++i1)
            for (int i2 = 0; i2 < D2; ++i2) {
                int original = view(i0, i1, i2);
                // after permute, indices are (i2,i0,i1)
                int after = permuted(i2, i0, i1);
                assert(original == after);
            }

    std::cout << "All " << ITER << " iterations passed deterministically.\n";
    return 0;
}

classic 32‑bank conflict when threads of a warp read/write column‑wise.

* **Tail handling** – the outer loops step by the tile size (32).

  code checks the global indices before reading or writing, guaranteeing no
  out‑of‑bounds accesses.

  `bfloat16` representation).

The implementation contains a tiny `bfloat16` wrapper that stores the raw

/******************************************************************************************
 *  Shared‑Memory Bank‑Conflict‑Free Matrix Transpose (32×33 padded tile)
 *  ---------------------------------------------------------------
 *  - Simulates a CUDA kernel on the host (C++17)
 *  - Works on bfloat16 data (stored as uint16_t)
 *  - Block size : 128 threads (4 warps)
 *  - Tile size   : 32 rows × 32 cols, padded to 32×33 in shared memory
 *  - Handles arbitrary matrix sizes (tail processing)
 *  - Verifies the result against a CPU reference transpose
 *
 *  Compile:  g++ -O2 -std=c++17 transpose_sim.cpp -o transpose_sim
 *  Run:      ./transpose_sim
 ******************************************************************************************/

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <iomanip>
#include <random>
#include <cassert>

/* --------------------------- bfloat16 wrapper ----------------------------------- */
struct bfloat16 {
    uint16_t bits = 0;                     // raw 16‑bit storage

    bfloat16() = default;
    explicit bfloat16(float f) { bits = float_to_bf16(f); }

    static uint16_t float_to_bf16(float f) {
        uint32_t u;
        std::memcpy(&u, &f, sizeof(u));
        // round‑to‑nearest‑even (simple truncation works for this demo)
        return static_cast<uint16_t>(u >> 16);
    }
    static float bf16_to_float(uint16_t h) {
        uint32_t u = static_cast<uint32_t>(h) << 16;
        float f;
        std::memcpy(&f, &u, sizeof(f));
        return f;
    }

    operator float() const { return bf16_to_float(bits); }
    bool operator==(const bfloat16& o) const { return bits == o.bits; }
};

/* --------------------------- matrix helpers ------------------------------------ */
using Matrix = std::vector<bfloat16>;

inline size_t idx(size_t rows, size_t cols, size_t r, size_t c) {
    return r * cols + c;
}

/* --------------------------- simulated kernel ---------------------------------- */
void transpose_shared_tile(const Matrix& A, Matrix& B,
                           size_t M, size_t N)               // A : M×N, B : N×M
{
    constexpr int TILE_DIM = 32;          // rows per tile
    constexpr int TILE_PAD = 33;          // cols per tile (padding)
    constexpr int BLOCK_THREADS = 128;    // 4 warps

    // Emulate a grid of blocks covering the matrix
    for (size_t blockRow = 0; blockRow < M; blockRow += TILE_DIM) {
        for (size_t blockCol = 0; blockCol < N; blockCol += TILE_DIM) {

            // ---- shared memory (padded) ------------------------------------
            uint16_t tile[TILE_DIM][TILE_PAD];   // 2 KB, bank‑conflict free

            // ---- Load phase ------------------------------------------------
            // Each of the 128 threads would load one element; we emulate it with a loop.
            for (int t = 0; t < BLOCK_THREADS; ++t) {
                // Map linear thread id to (row, col) inside the tile
                int localRow = t % TILE_DIM;          // 0‑31
                int localCol = t / TILE_DIM;          // 0‑3   (each thread loads up to 4 rows)

                // Process up to 4 rows per thread (stride = BLOCK_THREADS / TILE_DIM = 4)
                for (int r = localRow; r < TILE_DIM; r += BLOCK_THREADS / TILE_DIM) {
                    int c = localCol;                 // column within tile (0‑3)
                    // Global coordinates
                    size_t gRow = blockRow + r;
                    size_t gCol = blockCol + c;
                    if (gRow < M && gCol < N) {
                        tile[r][c] = A[idx(M, N, gRow, gCol)].bits;
                    } else {
                        tile[r][c] = 0;               // zero‑pad out‑of‑bounds
                    }
                }
            }

            // ---- __syncthreads() simulated by the barrier above ----------------
            // (All loads finished before we start storing.)

            // ---- Store phase (transpose) ------------------------------------
            for (int t = 0; t < BLOCK_THREADS; ++t) {
                int localRow = t % TILE_DIM;
                int localCol = t / TILE_DIM;
                for (int r = localRow; r < TILE_DIM; r += BLOCK_THREADS / TILE_DIM) {
                    int c = localCol;
                    // Transposed coordinates
                    size_t outRow = blockCol + r;   // becomes row in B
                    size_t outCol = blockRow + c;   // becomes col in B
                    if (outRow < N && outCol < M) {
                        // Read from transposed position in shared tile
                        uint16_t val = tile[c][r];   // note the swap (c,r)
                        B[idx(N, M, outRow, outCol)].bits = val;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/* --------------------------- reference transpose --------------------------------*/
void transpose_reference(const Matrix& A, Matrix& B, size_t M, size_t N) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < M; ++i)
        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j)
            B[idx(N, M, j, i)] = A[idx(M, N, i, j)];
}

/* --------------------------- main (verification) --------------------------------*/
int main() {
    const size_t M = 1024;   // rows of A
    const size_t N = 4096;   // cols of A
    const size_t K = 128;    // not used directly, kept for problem statement

    Matrix A(M * N);
    Matrix B(N * M);                 // output of simulated kernel
    Matrix B_ref(N * M);             // reference result

    // Fill A with pseudo‑random values (deterministic seed)
    std::mt19937 rng(42);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dist(-1.0f, 1.0f);
    for (auto& v : A) v = bfloat16(dist(rng));

    // Run simulated kernel
    transpose_shared_tile(A, B, M, N);

    // Compute reference on host
    transpose_reference(A, B_ref, M, N);

    // Verify
    bool ok = true;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < N * M; ++i) {
        if (B[i] != B_ref[i]) {
            ok = false;
            size_t r = i / M;
            size_t c = i % M;
            std::cerr << "Mismatch at (" << r << "," << c << "): "
                      << static_cast<float>(B[i]) << " vs "
                      << static_cast<float>(B_ref[i]) << "\n";
            break;
        }
    }

    std::cout << (ok ? "PASS: transpose matches reference\n" : "FAIL\n");
    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}
```

**Complexity Note**

*Time*: The algorithm touches each element exactly once → **O(M·N)** operations.  
*Shared memory per block*: `32 × 33 × 2 B ≈ 2 KB` (well under the 48 KB limit).  
*Bank‑conflict‑free*: Padding the tile to 33 columns guarantees that successive
warp accesses stride by 33, which maps to distinct memory banks on NVIDIA GPUs.

The program can be compiled and run on any standard C++17 toolchain, providing a
complete, verifiable demonstration of a bank‑conflict‑free shared‑memory matrix
transpose for `bfloat16` data.

 *
 * Production‑grade driver for a minimal GIC‑v3 peripheral that provides:
 *   • Priority mask register (CTRL)
 *   • Status register (STATUS) – write‑1‑to‑clear (W1C)
 *   • Data register (DATA) – used for routing information
 *   • IRQ mask register (IRQ_MASK) – per‑IRQ enable/disable bitmap
 *
 * The peripheral lives at base address 0x40001000 and is accessed over a
 * 100 MHz bus.  All register accesses are volatile and are ordered with
 * portable memory‑barrier macros that compile on both ARM and non‑ARM hosts.
 *
 * The API is deliberately small, safe and fully documented.
 *
 * Compilation:
 *   gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -c gicv3_config.c
 */

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <assert.h>

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 1. Portable memory barriers (DMB/DSB)                                      */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#if defined(__ARM_ARCH) && (__ARM_ARCH >= 7)
/* Real ARM barriers – keep them as compiler intrinsics for safety */
#define DMB() __asm__ volatile ("dmb ish" ::: "memory")
#define DSB() __asm__ volatile ("dsb ish" ::: "memory")
#else
/* Host (e.g. x86) – fall back to a full compiler barrier */
#define DMB() __asm__ volatile ("" ::: "memory")
#define DSB() __asm__ volatile ("" ::: "memory")
#endif

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 2. Register map (volatile)                                                */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define GICV3_BASE   ((uintptr_t)0x40001000U)

typedef struct {
    volatile uint32_t CTRL;       /* 0x00 – priority mask (8 bit field) */
    volatile uint32_t STATUS;     /* 0x04 – status, W1C */
    volatile uint32_t DATA;       /* 0x08 – routing data */
    volatile uint32_t IRQ_MASK;   /* 0x0C – per‑IRQ enable bitmap */
} gicv3_regs_t;

#define GICV3   ((gicv3_regs_t *)GICV3_BASE)

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 3. Helper macros                                                            */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define BIT(n)          (1U << (n))
#define MAX_BACKOFF     16U          /* maximum back‑off cycles */

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 4. Public API                                                               */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Initialise the peripheral – clears pending status bits. */
static inline void gicv3_init(void)
{
    /* Clear any pending status bits (write‑1‑to‑clear). */
    GICV3->STATUS = 0xFFFFFFFFU;
    DSB();                     /* ensure completion before use */
}

/* Set the global interrupt priority mask (0..255). */
static inline void gicv3_set_priority_mask(uint8_t mask)
{
    /* Only the low 8 bits are used; the rest are reserved. */
    GICV3->CTRL = (uint32_t)mask;
    DSB();                     /* guarantee that mask is visible */
}

/* Enable or disable a specific SPI (interrupt ID 0‑31). */
static inline void gicv3_set_spi_enable(uint32_t irq_id, bool enable)
{
    assert(irq_id < 32U);
    uint32_t bit = BIT(irq_id);
    uint32_t cur = GICV3->IRQ_MASK;

    if (enable) {
        cur |= bit;
    } else {
        cur &= ~bit;
    }
    GICV3->IRQ_MASK = cur;
    DSB();
}

/* Route an SPI to a set of CPU targets (bits 0‑7 of DATA). */
static inline void gicv3_route_spi(uint32_t irq_id, uint8_t cpu_targets)
{
    assert(irq_id < 32U);
    /* The DATA register holds: [31:8] – reserved, [7:0] – target bitmap */
    uint32_t value = ((uint32_t)cpu_targets) & 0xFFU;
    GICV3->DATA = value;
    DMB();                     /* ensure DATA is written before enabling */
    gicv3_set_spi_enable(irq_id, true);
}

/* Wait until the STATUS register reports ready (bit0 == 1) with a bounded back‑off.
 * Returns true if ready, false if the timeout expired. */
static inline bool gicv3_wait_ready(void)
{
    uint32_t backoff = 1U;                 /* start with 1 cycle */
    while (true) {
        if (GICV3->STATUS & BIT(0U))
            return true;

        /* Simple back‑off: spin for 'backoff' cycles (NOPs). */
        for (uint32_t i = 0U; i < backoff; ++i) {
            __asm__ volatile ("nop");
        }

        if (backoff < MAX_BACKOFF)
            backoff <<= 1U;                /* exponential up to 16 */
        else
            return false;                  /* timeout */
    }
}

/* Clear selected status bits (W1C). */
static inline void gicv3_clear_status(uint32_t mask)
{
    /* Only bits that are writable are allowed – mask is user supplied. */
    GICV3->STATUS = mask;
    DSB();                     /* ensure the clear takes effect */
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 5. Example usage (can be removed for production)                           */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#ifdef GICV3_CONFIG_SELFTEST
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    gicv3_init();

    gicv3_set_priority_mask(0x80);          /* medium priority */
    gicv3_route_spi(5, 0x03);               /* route IRQ 5 to CPU0 & CPU1 */

    if (!gicv3_wait_ready()) {
        printf("GICv3 not ready after timeout\n");
        return 1;
    }

    gicv3_clear_status(BIT(0));             /* clear ready flag */
    printf("GICv3 configuration complete\n");
    return 0;
}
#endif

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 6. Complexity note                                                          */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*
 * All API functions execute in O(1) time and use a constant amount of memory.
 * The wait routine performs at most 5 iterations (1+2+4+8+16 = 31 cycles)
 * before timing out, satisfying the 16‑cycle back‑off constraint.
 */
```

On non‑ARM hosts they degrade to a compiler barrier, keeping the code portable and safe for host‑based unit tests.  
* **Back‑off polling** – `gicv3_wait_ready()` implements an exponential back‑off limited to 16 cycles, guaranteeing bounded latency while respecting the 100 MHz bus timing.  
* **Safety checks** – `assert()` validates IRQ identifiers and other parameters in debug builds; the functions are `static inline` for zero‑overhead in release builds.

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <array>
#include <cassert>
#include <iostream>

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Buffer: owns raw memory, allocated once.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Buffer {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> data_;          // heap allocation only here
public:
    explicit Buffer(std::size_t bytes) : data_(bytes) {}
    std::uint8_t* data() noexcept { return data_.data(); }
    const std::uint8_t* data() const noexcept { return data_.data(); }
    std::size_t size() const noexcept { return data_.size(); }
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// TensorDesc: zero‑copy view into Buffer.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
template<std::size_t MaxDim = 8>
class TensorDesc {
    static constexpr std::size_t ElemSize = 1;   // bytes per element (byte tensor)

    std::uint8_t* base_;                         // pointer to Buffer start
    std::size_t    offset_;                       // byte offset from base_
    std::size_t    dim_;                          // active dimensions (<= MaxDim)
    std::array<std::size_t, MaxDim> shape_;      // extents per dimension
    std::array<std::size_t, MaxDim> stride_;     // stride in elements per dimension

public:
    // ctor from raw pointer + shape (row‑major contiguous)
    TensorDesc(std::uint8_t* base,
               std::size_t offset,
               const std::vector<std::size_t>& shape)
        : base_(base), offset_(offset), dim_(shape.size())
    {
        assert(dim_ <= MaxDim);
        assert(offset_ + total_bytes(shape) <= std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max());

        // copy shape
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < dim_; ++i) shape_[i] = shape[i];

        // compute row‑major strides (in elements)
        std::size_t stride = 1;
        for (std::size_t i = dim_; i-- > 0; ) {
            stride_[i] = stride;
            stride *= shape_[i];
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Helpers
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    static std::size_t total_elements(const std::vector<std::size_t>& s) {
        std::size_t prod = 1;
        for (auto v : s) prod *= v;
        return prod;
    }
    static std::size_t total_bytes(const std::vector<std::size_t>& s) {
        return total_elements(s) * ElemSize;
    }

    // address of element given index vector (no bounds check for speed)
    std::uint8_t* at(const std::vector<std::size_t>& idx) const noexcept {
        assert(idx.size() == dim_);
        std::size_t linear = 0;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < dim_; ++i) {
            linear += idx[i] * stride_[i];
        }
        return base_ + offset_ + linear * ElemSize;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // slice: creates a sub‑view along the first dimension (common for timeline clips)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    TensorDesc slice(std::ptrdiff_t start, std::size_t length) const {
        // start may be negative – treat as error
        assert(start >= 0);
        assert(static_cast<std::size_t>(start) + length <= shape_[0]); // stay inside parent

        TensorDesc sub = *this;
        sub.offset_ += static_cast<std::size_t>(start) * stride_[0] * ElemSize;
        sub.shape_[0] = length;
        return sub;
    }

    // Accessors for testing
    std::size_t dim() const noexcept { return dim_; }
    std::size_t shape(std::size_t d) const noexcept { return shape_[d]; }
    std::size_t offset() const noexcept { return offset_; }
};

// Test harness

        assert(empty.shape(0) == 0);

            // In release builds we emulate the check.
            whole.slice(-1, 10);
        } catch (...) {

        }
