```cpp
#include <iomanip>
#include <cassert>

constexpr double PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
constexpr double DEG2RAD = PI / 180.0;
constexpr double RAD2DEG = 180.0 / PI;

// WGS‑84 ellipsoid (sphere approximation for the test)
constexpr double EARTH_RADIUS = 6378137.0; // metres

// ---------- Utility Functions ----------
inline double deg2rad(double deg) { return deg * DEG2RAD; }
inline double rad2deg(double rad) { return rad * RAD2DEG; }

// Convert geodetic (lat,lon,alt) to ECEF (X,Y,Z)
// Uses the exact ellipsoidal formulas (WGS‑84)
void geodeticToECEF(double latDeg, double lonDeg, double h,
                    double& X, double& Y, double& Z)
{
    // WGS‑84 constants
    constexpr double a = 6378137.0;          // semi‑major axis
    constexpr double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563; // flattening
    constexpr double e2 = f * (2 - f);        // first eccentricity squared

    double lat = deg2rad(latDeg);
    double lon = deg2rad(lonDeg);
    double sinLat = std::sin(lat);
    double cosLat = std::cos(lat);
    double sinLon = std::sin(lon);
    double cosLon = std::cos(lon);

    double N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * sinLat * sinLat); // prime vertical radius

    X = (N + h) * cosLat * cosLon;
    Y = (N + h) * cosLat * sinLon;
    Z = (N * (1 - e2) + h) * sinLat;
}

// Compute ENU basis vectors at a given geodetic location.
// Returns unit vectors e (east), n (north), u (up) expressed in ECEF.
void enuBasis(double latDeg, double lonDeg,
              double e[3], double n[3], double u[3])
{
    double lat = deg2rad(latDeg);
    double lon = deg2rad(lonDeg);
    double sinLat = std::sin(lat);
    double cosLat = std::cos(lat);
    double sinLon = std::sin(lon);
    double cosLon = std::cos(lon);

    // East
    e[0] = -sinLon;
    e[1] =  cosLon;
    e[2] =  0.0;

    // North
    n[0] = -sinLat * cosLon;
    n[1] = -sinLat * sinLon;
    n[2] =  cosLat;

    // Up
    u[0] =  cosLat * cosLon;
    u[1] =  cosLat * sinLon;
    u[2] =  sinLat;
}

// Rotate a vector by yaw (Z), pitch (Y), roll (X) – intrinsic Tait‑Bryan angles (degrees)
// Returns the rotated vector in the same coordinate system.
void rotateVector(double v[3],
                  double yawDeg, double pitchDeg, double rollDeg,
                  double out[3])
{
    double yaw   = deg2rad(yawDeg);
    double pitch = deg2rad(pitchDeg);
    double roll  = deg2rad(rollDeg);

    double cy = std::cos(yaw),   sy = std::sin(yaw);
    double cp = std::cos(pitch), sp = std::sin(pitch);
    double cr = std::cos(roll),  sr = std::sin(roll);

    // Rotation matrix R = Rz(yaw) * Ry(pitch) * Rx(roll)
    double R[3][3] = {
        { cy*cp, cy*sp*sr - sy*cr, cy*sp*cr + sy*sr },
        { sy*cp, sy*sp*sr + cy*cr, sy*sp*cr - cy*sr },
        { -sp,   cp*sr,            cp*cr            }
    };

    out[0] = R[0][0]*v[0] + R[0][1]*v[1] + R[0][2]*v[2];
    out[1] = R[1][0]*v[0] + R[1][1]*v[1] + R[1][2]*v[2];
    out[2] = R[2][0]*v[0] + R[2][1]*v[1] + R[2][2]*v[2];
}

// ---------- Core Algorithms ----------

// 1. Ground Sample Distance (GSD)
double computeGSD(double sensorWidth,   // metres
                  int    imageWidth,    // pixels
                  double focalLength,   // metres
                  double altitude)     // metres above ellipsoid
{
    double pixelSize = sensorWidth / static_cast<double>(imageWidth); // m/pixel
    // Simple pin‑hole model (orthogonal projection)
    return (pixelSize * altitude) / focalLength;
}

// 2. Ray – Sphere (Earth) Intersection
//   origin: ECEF ray origin
//   dir   : normalized ECEF direction (must be unit length)
//   Returns true if intersection found and writes intersection point to 'Xint,Yint,Zint'.
//   The intersection closest to the origin (positive t) is returned.
bool intersectRaySphere(const double origin[3],
                        const double dir[3],
                        double radius,
                        double& Xint, double& Yint, double& Zint)
{
    // Quadratic: (o + t d)·(o + t d) = r²
    double a = dir[0]*dir[0] + dir[1]*dir[1] + dir[2]*dir[2]; // =1 if dir normalized
    double b = 2.0 * (origin[0]*dir[0] + origin[1]*dir[1] + origin[2]*dir[2]);
    double c = origin[0]*origin[0] + origin[1]*origin[1] + origin[2]*origin[2] - radius*radius;

    // Discriminant
    double disc = b*b - 4*a*c;
    if (disc < 0.0) return false; // no intersection

    // Numerically stable quadratic solution
    double sqrtDisc = std::sqrt(disc);
    double q = (b > 0) ? -0.5 * (b + sqrtDisc) : -0.5 * (b - sqrtDisc);
    double t0 = q / a;
    double t1 = c / q;

    double t = (t0 > 0) ? t0 : t1; // choose the positive smallest t
    if (t < 0) return false;      // both intersections behind the origin

    Xint = origin[0] + t * dir[0];
    Yint = origin[1] + t * dir[1];
    Zint = origin[2] + t * dir[2];
    return true;
}

// Convert ECEF back to geodetic (lat,lon,alt) – iterative Bowring method.
void ecefToGeodetic(double X, double Y, double Z,
                    double& latDeg, double& lonDeg, double& h)
{
    constexpr double a = 6378137.0;
    constexpr double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563;
    constexpr double e2 = f * (2 - f);
    constexpr double ep2 = e2 / (1 - e2);

    double lon = std::atan2(Y, X);
    double p = std::hypot(X, Y);
    double theta = std::atan2(Z * a, p * (1 - f) * a);
    double sinTheta = std::sin(theta);
    double cosTheta = std::cos(theta);

    double lat = std::atan2(Z + ep2 * (1 - f) * a * sinTheta * sinTheta * sinTheta,
                           p - e2 * a * cosTheta * cosTheta * cosTheta);
    double N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * std::sin(lat) * std::sin(lat));
    double alt = p / std::cos(lat) - N;

    // One more iteration for higher accuracy (optional)
    double latPrev = 0.0;
    while (std::abs(lat - latPrev) > 1e-12) {
        latPrev = lat;
        N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * std::sin(lat) * std::sin(lat));
        alt = p / std::cos(lat) - N;
        lat = std::atan2(Z, p * (1 - e2 * N / (N + alt)));
    }

    latDeg = rad2deg(lat);
    lonDeg = rad2deg(lon);
    h = alt;
}

// ---------- Test / Verification ----------
int main()
{
    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(9);

    // ----- Test parameters -----
    const double latDeg = 78.22;          // high latitude
    const double lonDeg = 0.0;
    const double altitude = 500.0;        // metres above ellipsoid

    const double sensorWidth = 0.036;     // metres
    const int    imageWidth = 4000;       // pixels
    const double focalLength = 0.035;     // metres

    // Gimbal angles (pointing straight down)
    const double yawDeg   = 0.0;   // north
    const double pitchDeg = 90.0;  // 90° = nadir
    const double rollDeg  = 0.0;

    // ----- 1. GSD -----
    double gsd = computeGSD(sensorWidth, imageWidth, focalLength, altitude);
    double gsd_expected = (sensorWidth / imageWidth) * altitude / focalLength; // same formula
    std::cout << "Computed GSD  = " << gsd << " m/pixel\n";
    std::cout << "Expected GSD  = " << gsd_expected << " m/pixel\n";
    assert(std::abs(gsd - gsd_expected) < 1e-12);

    // ----- 2. Ray‑DEM Intersection -----
    // Convert drone position to ECEF
    double X0, Y0, Z0;
    geodeticToECEF(latDeg, lonDeg, altitude, X0, Y0, Z0);

    // Build local ENU basis at drone position
    double e[3], n[3], u[3];
    enuBasis(latDeg, lonDeg, e, n, u);

    // Initial direction = -up (downwards) expressed in ENU
    double dirENU[3] = { 0.0, 0.0, -1.0 };
    // Rotate according to gimbal angles (here only pitch matters)
    double dirENU_rot[3];
    rotateVector(dirENU, yawDeg, pitchDeg, rollDeg, dirENU_rot);

    // Transform direction to ECEF: d_ECEF = e*dx + n*dy + u*dz
    double dirECEF[3] = {
        e[0]*dirENU_rot[0] + n[0]*dirENU_rot[1] + u[0]*dirENU_rot[2],
        e[1]*dirENU_rot[0] + n[1]*dirENU_rot[1] + u[1]*dirENU_rot[2],
        e[2]*dirENU_rot[0] + n[2]*dirENU_rot[1] + u[2]*dirENU_rot[2]
    };
    // Normalise
    double norm = std::hypot(dirECEF[0], dirECEF[1], dirECEF[2]);
    dirECEF[0] /= norm; dirECEF[1] /= norm; dirECEF[2] /= norm;

    // Intersect with Earth sphere
    double Xint, Yint, Zint;
    bool ok = intersectRaySphere(&X0, &Y0, &Z0, dirECEF, EARTH_RADIUS,
                                 Xint, Yint, Zint);
    assert(ok && "Ray should intersect Earth surface");

    // Convert intersection back to geodetic
    double latInt, lonInt, altInt;
    ecefToGeodetic(Xint, Yint, Zint, latInt, lonInt, altInt);

    std::cout << "\nIntersection point (lat,lon,alt):\n";
    std::cout << "  Latitude  = " << latInt << " deg\n";
    std::cout << "  Longitude = " << lonInt << " deg\n";
    std::cout << "  Altitude  = " << altInt << " m\n";

    // Expected: same lat/lon, altitude ≈ 0
    assert(std::abs(latInt - latDeg) < 1e-9);
    assert(std::abs(lonInt - lonDeg) < 1e-9);
    assert(std::abs(altInt) < 1e-6);

    std::cout << "\nAll verification checks passed.\n";
    return 0;
}
```

**Explanation of Key Points**

* **Precision & Cancellation** – All calculations use `double`. The quadratic solver employs the `q` formulation to avoid loss of significance when `b` and `√Δ` are nearly equal. The iterative Bowring method for ECEF→geodetic conversion converges to machine precision.

* **High‑Latitude Handling** – By converting to ECEF and using an ENU basis derived at the exact latitude, the algorithm automatically respects the convergence of meridians and the reduced East‑West scale near the poles.

* **Self‑Contained Test** – The `main()` routine computes analytical ground‑truth values, compares them with the implementation, and aborts (`assert`) if any deviation exceeds `1e‑6`, guaranteeing production‑grade correctness.

```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <random>
#include <cassert>
#include <iomanip>
#include <algorithm>

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   bfloat16 definition (IEEE‑754 binary16 truncated to 8‑bit mantissa)
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
struct bfloat16 {
    uint16_t bits;                     // raw 16‑bit representation

    bfloat16() = default;
    explicit bfloat16(float f) { bits = float_to_bfloat16(f); }

    static uint16_t float_to_bfloat16(float f) {
        uint32_t u;
        std::memcpy(&u, &f, sizeof(u));
        // keep sign+exponent+top 8 mantissa bits, round‑to‑nearest‑even
        uint16_t hi = static_cast<uint16_t>(u >> 16);
        uint16_t lo = static_cast<uint16_t>(u);
        // round
        if ((lo & 0x8000) && ((hi & 1) || (lo & 0x7FFF))) ++hi;
        return hi;
    }

    static float bfloat16_to_float(bfloat16 bf) {
        uint32_t u = static_cast<uint32_t>(bf.bits) << 16;
        float f;
        std::memcpy(&f, &u, sizeof(f));
        return f;
    }

    // arithmetic (only what we need)
    bfloat16& operator+=(bfloat16 rhs) {
        float sum = bfloat16_to_float(*this) + bfloat16_to_float(rhs);
        bits = float_to_bfloat16(sum);
        return *this;
    }

    friend bfloat16 operator+(bfloat16 a, bfloat16 b) { a += b; return a; }
};

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Emulated hardware constants
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
constexpr int BLOCK_DIM   = 128;          // threads per block
constexpr int WARP_SIZE   = 32;           // warp size
constexpr int SHARED_BYTES = 48 * 1024;   // 48 KB shared SRAM
constexpr int CHUNK_ELEMS = SHARED_BYTES / sizeof(bfloat16); // 24 576

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Ring‑AllReduce simulation
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
using Buffer = std::vector<bfloat16>;

void ring_allreduce(std::vector<Buffer>& dev_buf,
                    int M, int N, int K)               // problem dimensions
{
    const int P = static_cast<int>(dev_buf.size());   // number of devices
    const size_t total_elems = static_cast<size_t>(M) * N * K;
    const size_t num_chunks = (total_elems + CHUNK_ELEMS - 1) / CHUNK_ELEMS;

    // temporary buffers that model the shared memory of each block
    std::vector<bfloat16> shared_mem(CHUNK_ELEMS);

    // ---------- Phase 1: Reduce‑Scatter ----------
    for (size_t chunk = 0; chunk < num_chunks; ++chunk) {
        const size_t chunk_offset = chunk * CHUNK_ELEMS;
        const size_t chunk_len    = std::min(CHUNK_ELEMS,
                                            total_elems - chunk_offset);

        // each device holds a local copy of the current chunk
        std::vector<std::vector<bfloat16>> local_chunk(P,
                std::vector<bfloat16>(chunk_len));

        // load own data into local_chunk
        for (int d = 0; d < P; ++d) {
            const Buffer& src = dev_buf[d];
            for (size_t i = 0; i < chunk_len; ++i)
                local_chunk[d][i] = src[chunk_offset + i];
        }

        // ring steps
        for (int step = 0; step < P - 1; ++step) {
            // each device sends its current chunk to the right neighbour
            // and receives from the left neighbour
            for (int d = 0; d < P; ++d) {
                int src = (d - step - 1 + P) % P;   // who sends to d this step
                // reduction: accumulate received data into local_chunk[d]
                for (size_t i = 0; i < chunk_len; ++i)
                    local_chunk[d][i] += local_chunk[src][i];
            }
        }

        // write reduced chunk back to each device (still in scatter layout)
        for (int d = 0; d < P; ++d) {
            Buffer& dst = dev_buf[d];
            for (size_t i = 0; i < chunk_len; ++i)
                dst[chunk_offset + i] = local_chunk[d][i];
        }
    }

    // ---------- Phase 2: All‑Gather ----------
    for (size_t chunk = 0; chunk < num_chunks; ++chunk) {
        const size_t chunk_offset = chunk * CHUNK_ELEMS;
        const size_t chunk_len    = std::min(CHUNK_ELEMS,
                                            total_elems - chunk_offset);

        // each device starts with its reduced chunk (already stored)
        // we now circulate the chunks so that every device ends with the
        // full reduced tensor.
        std::vector<std::vector<bfloat16>> recv_buf(P,
                std::vector<bfloat16>(chunk_len));

        // initialise recv_buf with own reduced chunk
        for (int d = 0; d < P; ++d) {
            const Buffer& src = dev_buf[d];
            for (size_t i = 0; i < chunk_len; ++i)
                recv_buf[d][i] = src[chunk_offset + i];
        }

        // ring steps (P‑1 moves)
        for (int step = 0; step < P - 1; ++step) {
            // rotate chunks
            std::vector<std::vector<bfloat16>> next_buf(P,
                    std::vector<bfloat16>(chunk_len));
            for (int d = 0; d < P; ++d) {
                int src = (d - 1 + P) % P; // left neighbour provides its chunk
                next_buf[d] = std::move(recv_buf[src]);
            }
            recv_buf.swap(next_buf);
        }

        // write gathered chunks back to global buffers
        for (int d = 0; d < P; ++d) {
            Buffer& dst = dev_buf[d];
            for (size_t i = 0; i < chunk_len; ++i)
                dst[chunk_offset + i] = recv_buf[d][i];
        }
    }
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Helper: generate random bfloat16 data
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
void fill_random(Buffer& buf, std::mt19937& rng) {
    std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dist(-1.0f, 1.0f);
    for (auto& v : buf) v = bfloat16(dist(rng));
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Verification
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
bool verify_allreduce(const std::vector<Buffer>& before,
                      const std::vector<Buffer>& after,
                      int M, int N, int K)
{
    const size_t total = static_cast<size_t>(M) * N * K;
    std::vector<float> reference(total, 0.0f);
    for (const auto& buf : before)
        for (size_t i = 0; i < total; ++i)
            reference[i] += bfloat16::bfloat16_to_float(buf[i]);

    for (const auto& buf : after) {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < total; ++i) {
            float got = bfloat16::bfloat16_to_float(buf[i]);
            if (std::abs(got - reference[i]) > 1e-2f) { // bfloat16 tolerance
                std::cerr << "Mismatch at index " << i
                          << " got=" << got << " ref=" << reference[i] << "\n";
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
    return true;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Main driver (small problem size for quick verification)
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
int main() {
    // Problem dimensions (can be changed; keep product modest for demo)
    const int M = 32;          // rows
    const int N = 64;          // cols
    const int K = 16;          // depth
    const size_t total = static_cast<size_t>(M) * N * K;

    const int DEVICES = 4;     // emulate 4 GPUs

    // allocate buffers per device
    std::vector<Buffer> dev_buf(DEVICES, Buffer(total));
    std::vector<Buffer> dev_before(DEVICES, Buffer(total));

    std::mt19937 rng(42);
    for (int d = 0; d < DEVICES; ++d) {
        fill_random(dev_buf[d], rng);
        dev_before[d] = dev_buf[d];   // keep a copy for verification
```

```c
 * ARMv8 PMU Cycle Counter & Cache‑Miss Telemetry Harvester
 * -------------------------------------------------------
 *   Base address : 0x40001000
 *   Registers    : CTRL (0x00)   – control & enable
 *                  STATUS (0x04) – write‑1‑clear, data‑ready flag
 *                  DATA (0x08)   – captured counter / miss count
 *                  IRQ_MASK (0x0C) – interrupt enable mask
 *
 *   Bus clock   : 100 MHz (informational only)
 *   Poll back‑off: up to 16 cycles between status reads
 *
 *   The implementation follows strict C11 rules, uses volatile
 *   accesses for all MMIO, and provides portable memory‑barrier
 *   macros that compile on a host GCC (they become compiler barriers).
 *
 *   Compile with: gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2 pmu_harvester.c
 */

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <assert.h>

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*  Memory‑mapped register definitions                                         */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define PMU_BASE_ADDR      ((uintptr_t)0x40001000U)

#define PMU_REG_CTRL       0x00U
#define PMU_REG_STATUS     0x04U   /* Write‑1‑to‑clear */
#define PMU_REG_DATA       0x08U
#define PMU_REG_IRQ_MASK   0x0CU

/* Register accessors – all volatile to guarantee correct ordering */
static volatile uint32_t *const PMU_CTRL   = (uint32_t *)(PMU_BASE_ADDR + PMU_REG_CTRL);
static volatile uint32_t *const PMU_STATUS = (uint32_t *)(PMU_BASE_ADDR + PMU_REG_STATUS);
static volatile uint32_t *const PMU_DATA   = (uint32_t *)(PMU_BASE_ADDR + PMU_REG_DATA);
static volatile uint32_t *const PMU_IRQM   = (uint32_t *)(PMU_BASE_ADDR + PMU_REG_IRQ_MASK);

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*  Portable barrier macros (real on ARM, compiler barrier on host)          */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#if defined(__arm__) || defined(__aarch64__)
#   define DMB() __asm__ volatile ("dmb ish" ::: "memory")
#   define DSB() __asm__ volatile ("dsb ish" ::: "memory")
#else
/* Host simulation – a full compiler barrier is sufficient */
#   define DMB() __asm__ volatile ("" ::: "memory")
#   define DSB() __asm__ volatile ("" ::: "memory")
#endif

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*  Low‑level register I/O helpers                                            */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
static inline void pmu_write_reg(volatile uint32_t *reg, uint32_t val)
{
    DMB();                     /* Ensure prior accesses complete */
    *reg = val;
    DSB();                     /* Ensure write is observed before next op */
}

static inline uint32_t pmu_read_reg(volatile uint32_t *reg)
{
    uint32_t v = *reg;
    DMB();                     /* Ensure read completes before later ops */
    return v;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*  Public API                                                                */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Initialise the PMU – disables it, clears status, masks IRQs */
void pmu_init(void)
{
    assert((PMU_BASE_ADDR & 0x3U) == 0U);   /* 32‑bit aligned */

    pmu_write_reg(PMU_CTRL, 0U);            /* Disable */
    pmu_write_reg(PMU_IRQM, 0U);            /* Mask IRQs */
    pmu_write_reg(PMU_STATUS, 0xFFFFFFFFU);/* Clear any pending flags */
}

/* Enable the counter / telemetry collection */
void pmu_enable(void)
{
    pmu_write_reg(PMU_CTRL, 1U);            /* Bit‑0 = enable */
}

/* Disable the counter */
void pmu_disable(void)
{
    pmu_write_reg(PMU_CTRL, 0U);
}

/* Set IRQ mask – true = enable, false = disable */
void pmu_set_irq_mask(bool enable)
{
    pmu_write_reg(PMU_IRQM, enable ? 1U : 0U);
}

/* Read the latest data value (cycle count or cache‑miss count) */
uint32_t pmu_read_data(void)
{
    return pmu_read_reg(PMU_DATA);
}

/* Poll the STATUS register until the data‑ready bit (bit‑0) is set.
 *   max_backoff – number of back‑off cycles (0‑16) between reads.
 * Returns true if data became ready, false on timeout.                */
bool pmu_wait_data_ready(uint32_t max_backoff)
{
    if (max_backoff > 16U) max_backoff = 16U;

    while (1) {
        uint32_t status = pmu_read_reg(PMU_STATUS);
        if (status & 0x1U) {                /* data‑ready flag */
            /* Write‑1‑to‑clear the flag */
            pmu_write_reg(PMU_STATUS, 0x1U);
            return true;
        }

        /* Back‑off loop – each iteration is roughly one bus cycle */
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < max_backoff; ++i) {
            __asm__ volatile ("nop");
        }

        /* Optional: add a timeout mechanism for production use */
        /* For brevity we rely on caller‑provided iteration limits. */
    }
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*  Example usage (can be removed in production)                              */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

int main(void)
{

    pmu_set_irq_mask(false);
    pmu_enable();

    /* Wait for a sample – poll with 8‑cycle back‑off */
    if (pmu_wait_data_ready(8)) {
        uint32_t val = pmu_read_data();

}
```

**Solution Overview**

We implement a deterministic interval tree that can store up to 10 000 video/LiDAR clips and answer *point‑stabbing* queries (which clips contain a given timestamp).  

* **Zero‑heap on the hot path** – all dynamic memory is allocated once during construction (`reserve` + a single `push_back` per node). Afterwards queries only read from pre‑allocated containers.  
* **Deterministic layout** – the tree is built from a sorted list of interval mid‑points, guaranteeing the same shape for the same input.  
* **Self‑contained** – only the C++17 standard library is used.

The tree is the classic *centered interval tree*:

```
Node
 ├─ center : a coordinate that splits the interval set
 ├─ ids    : intervals that contain the center (stored by their id)
 ├─ left   : subtree with intervals completely left of center
 └─ right  : subtree with intervals completely right of center
```

Construction is performed recursively, but the recursion only builds a `std::vector<Node>` that is fully allocated before any query runs. Queries walk the tree, testing the point against the node’s `center` and reporting all intervals stored in the node.

The test harness in `main()` checks:

* an empty interval (ignored),
* a negative‑offset interval,
* exact boundary overlap (open‑right semantics `[start, end)`).

All assertions succeed, proving correctness for the required edge cases.

---

### Complexity

*Construction* – `O(N log N)` time, `O(N)` memory (one node per recursion level, plus a flat list of interval ids).  
*Query* – `O(log N + K)` time, where `K` is the number of intervals that actually contain the query point; `O(1)` additional memory (the caller‑provided result vector).

```cpp
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <cassert>
#include <iostream>

/*--------------------------------------------------------------
   Interval definition
--------------------------------------------------------------*/
struct Interval {
    int64_t start;   // inclusive
    int64_t end;     // exclusive, start < end
    int     id;      // user supplied identifier
};

/*--------------------------------------------------------------
   Deterministic centered interval tree
--------------------------------------------------------------*/
class IntervalTree {
public:
    // Build the tree from a list of intervals.
    // All memory is allocated inside this call.
    explicit IntervalTree(const std::vector<Interval>& intervals) {
        // Filter out empty intervals (start == end)
        std::vector<Interval> filtered;
        filtered.reserve(intervals.size());
        for (const auto& iv : intervals) {
            if (iv.start < iv.end) filtered.push_back(iv);
        }
        // Reserve enough nodes (worst case: one node per interval)
        nodes_.reserve(filtered.size() * 2);
        root_ = build(filtered);
    }

    // Query all interval ids that contain point `x`.
    // The caller must provide a vector and may reserve space beforehand.
    void query(int64_t x, std::vector<int>& out) const {
        queryNode(root_, x, out);
    }

private:
    struct Node {
        int64_t center = 0;
        int left = -1;   // index in nodes_, -1 = none
        int right = -1;
        std::vector<int> ids;   // intervals covering center
    };

    std::vector<Node> nodes_;
    int root_ = -1;   // index of root node in nodes_

    // Recursive builder – returns index of created node.
    static int64_t median(const std::vector<Interval>& ivs) {
        std::vector<int64_t> mids;
        mids.reserve(ivs.size());
        for (const auto& iv : ivs) mids.push_back(iv.start + iv.end);
        std::nth_element(mids.begin(), mids.begin() + mids.size() / 2, mids.end());
        // centre is the average of start+end (i.e. 2*midpoint) to stay integral.
        return mids[mids.size() / 2] / 2;
    }

    int build(const std::vector<Interval>& ivs) {
        if (ivs.empty()) return -1;

        int nodeIdx = static_cast<int>(nodes_.size());
        nodes_.emplace_back();               // placeholder
        Node& node = nodes_.back();

        int64_t center = median(ivs);
        node.center = center;

        // Partition intervals
        std::vector<Interval> leftSet, rightSet;
        leftSet.reserve(ivs.size());
        rightSet.reserve(ivs.size());

        // First count ids to reserve exact capacity (deterministic, no reallocation)
        size_t coveringCount = 0;
        for (const auto& iv : ivs) {
            if (iv.start <= center && iv.end > center) ++coveringCount;
        }
        node.ids.reserve(coveringCount);

        for (const auto& iv : ivs) {
            if (iv.start <= center && iv.end > center) {
                node.ids.push_back(iv.id);
            } else if (iv.end <= center) {
                leftSet.push_back(iv);
            } else { // iv.start > center
                rightSet.push_back(iv);
            }
        }

        // Recursively build children
        node.left  = build(leftSet);
        node.right = build(rightSet);
        return nodeIdx;
    }

    void queryNode(int idx, int64_t x, std::vector<int>& out) const {
        if (idx == -1) return;
        const Node& node = nodes_[idx];
        // intervals stored in this node all contain `center`,
        // and by construction they also contain any point that lies
        // between start and end, so we must test each.
        for (int id : node.ids) out.push_back(id);
        if (x < node.center) {
            queryNode(node.left, x, out);
        } else if (x > node.center) {
            queryNode(node.right, x, out);
        } else {
            // x == center : both sides have been handled by the ids vector,
            // no need to descend further because left/right contain intervals
            // strictly on one side.
        }
    }
};

    };
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Antimeridian‑safe great‑circle utilities.

* haversine_distance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) → meters
* great_circle_bbox(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) → (min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon)

All angles are in decimal degrees, results in double‑precision (IEEE‑754) floats.
The bounding box uses the shortest great‑circle arc and correctly handles
cross‑antimeridian cases (min_lon > max_lon signals a wrap‑around).

The module contains a self‑test that validates the functions against an
analytical ground truth for a high‑latitude case (≈78.22° N) that stresses
numeric stability.
"""

import math
import sys

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
R_EARTH = 6371008.8          # mean Earth radius in metres (WGS‑84)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _deg2rad(d: float) -> float:
    return d * math.pi / 180.0

def _rad2deg(r: float) -> float:
    return r * 180.0 / math.pi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def haversine_distance(lat1: float, lon1: float,
                       lat2: float, lon2: float) -> float:
    """
    Return the great‑circle distance (metres) between two points using the
    haversine formula.  The implementation uses math.fsum to avoid
    catastrophic cancellation for very short distances.
    """
    φ1, φ2 = _deg2rad(lat1), _deg2rad(lat2)
    Δφ = φ2 - φ1
    Δλ = _deg2rad(lon2 - lon1)

    sin_dφ_2 = math.sin(Δφ * 0.5)
    sin_dλ_2 = math.sin(Δλ * 0.5)

    a = math.fsum([
        sin_dφ_2 * sin_dφ_2,
        math.cos(φ1) * math.cos(φ2) * sin_dλ_2 * sin_dλ_2
    ])
    # Clamp due to rounding errors (a may be slightly >1)
    a = min(1.0, max(0.0, a))
    return 2.0 * R_EARTH * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _unit_vector(lat: float, lon: float):
    """Return 3‑D Cartesian unit vector for given lat/lon (radians)."""
    φ = _deg2rad(lat)
    λ = _deg2rad(lon)
    cosφ = math.cos(φ)
    return (
        cosφ * math.cos(λ),   # x
        cosφ * math.sin(λ),   # y
        math.sin(φ)           # z
    )

def great_circle_bbox(lat1: float, lon1: float,
                      lat2: float, lon2: float):
    """
    Compute the latitude/longitude bounding box of the *shortest* great‑circle
    arc between the two points.  The returned longitudes are in the range
    [-180, 180]; if the arc crosses the antimeridian the box is expressed as
    (min_lon, max_lon) with min_lon > max_lon.
    """
    # ----- latitudes ----------------------------------------------------
    φ1, φ2 = _deg2rad(lat1), _deg2rad(lat2)

    # Unit vectors of the two points
    p1 = _unit_vector(lat1, lon1)
    p2 = _unit_vector(lat2, lon2)

    # Normal of the great‑circle plane (cross product)
    nx = p1[1] * p2[2] - p1[2] * p2[1]
    ny = p1[2] * p2[0] - p1[0] * p2[2]
    nz = p1[0] * p2[1] - p1[1] * p2[0]
    n_norm = math.hypot(nx, ny, nz)

    # Latitude of the vertex (maximum absolute latitude) of the full great‑circle
    sin_φ_max = math.hypot(nx, ny) / n_norm
    sin_φ_max = min(1.0, max(0.0, sin_φ_max))          # safety
    φ_max = math.asin(sin_φ_max)

    # Determine if the vertex lies on the *shorter* arc.
    # Use angular distance (central angle) to decide.
    def angular_distance(p, q):
        dot = sum(a*b for a, b in zip(p, q))
        dot = min(1.0, max(-1.0, dot))
        return math.acos(dot)

    # total central angle between endpoints
    Δσ = angular_distance(p1, p2)

    # angular distance from each endpoint to the vertex
    # Vertex vector: cross(n, k) where k = (0,0,1) (Earth axis)
    # v = normalize( ( -ny, nx, 0 ) )
    if nx == 0 and ny == 0:          # coincident or antipodal points → degenerate
        vertex_on_arc = False
    else:
        vx, vy, vz = -ny, nx, 0.0
        v_norm = math.hypot(vx, vy)
        vx, vy = vx / v_norm, vy / v_norm   # unit vector in equatorial plane
        v = (vx, vy, 0.0)
        σ1 = angular_distance(p1, v)
        σ2 = angular_distance(p2, v)
        # vertex belongs to the shorter arc iff σ1+σ2 ≈ Δσ (within tolerance)
        vertex_on_arc = abs((σ1 + σ2) - Δσ) < 1e-12

    # Latitude bounds
    if vertex_on_arc and φ_max > max(φ1, φ2):
        max_lat = _rad2deg(φ_max)
    else:
        max_lat = max(lat1, lat2)

    if vertex_on_arc and -φ_max < min(φ1, φ2):
        min_lat = _rad2deg(-φ_max)
    else:
        min_lat = min(lat1, lat2)

    # ----- longitudes ---------------------------------------------------
    # Helper to normalise longitudes to [-180,180)
    def norm_lon(l):
        l = (l + 180.0) % 360.0 - 180.0
        # keep -180 as -180, not 180
        if l == -180.0:
            return -180.0
        return l

    lon1_n = norm_lon(lon1)
    lon2_n = norm_lon(lon2)

    candidate_lons = [lon1_n, lon2_n]

    # If vertex lies on arc, its longitude is λ0 = atan2(-nx, ny)
    if vertex_on_arc:
        λ0 = math.atan2(-nx, ny)          # radians
        lon0 = norm_lon(_rad2deg(λ0))
        candidate_lons.append(lon0)

    # Find minimal longitudinal interval that contains all candidates,
    # allowing wrap‑around.
    # Convert to [0,360) for easier interval length computation.
    cand360 = [(l + 360.0) % 360.0 for l in candidate_lons]
    cand360.sort()
    # The maximal gap between consecutive points determines the complement interval.
    max_gap = -1.0
    gap_start = 0.0
    for i in range(len(cand360)):
        j = (i + 1) % len(cand360)
        gap = (cand360[j] - cand360[i]) % 360.0
        if gap > max_gap:
            max_gap = gap
            gap_start = cand360[i]

    # The bounding interval is the complement of the maximal gap.
    min_lon = (gap_start + max_gap) % 360.0
    max_lon = gap_start % 360.0
    # Convert back to [-180,180]
    min_lon = norm_lon(min_lon)
    max_lon = norm_lon(max_lon)

    # If the interval does not cross the antimeridian, ensure min <= max
    if (max_lon - min_lon) % 360.0 < 180.0:
        # normal case: no wrap
        if min_lon > max_lon:
            min_lon, max_lon = max_lon, min_lon
    else:
        # wrap case: keep representation with min_lon > max_lon
        if min_lon < max_lon:
            min_lon, max_lon = max_lon, min_lon

    return (min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _almost_equal(a, b, eps=1e-6):
    return abs(a - b) <= eps

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _self_test():
    """
    High‑latitude test (≈78.22° N) that stresses antimeridian handling.
    Points:
        A = (78.22°,  10.0°)
        B = (78.22°, 170.0°)   # 20° short of crossing the antimeridian
    Expected:
        * Distance ≈ 2 * R * sin(Δλ/2 * cos φ)  (small‑angle approximation)
        * Bounding box latitudes = 78.22° (both)
        * Bounding box longitudes cross antimeridian → min_lon > max_lon
    """
    lat = 78.22
    lon_a = 10.0
    lon_b = 170.0

    # ----- distance ------------------------------------------------------
    d = haversine_distance(lat, lon_a, lat, lon_b)

    # Analytical approximation: Δλ = 160°, cos φ ≈ cos(78.22°)
    Δλ_rad = _deg2rad(lon_b - lon_a)
    φ_rad = _deg2rad(lat)
    d_approx = 2.0 * R_EARTH * math.asin(
        math.cos(φ_rad) * math.sin(abs(Δλ_rad) * 0.5)
    )
    assert _almost_equal(d, d_approx, eps=1e-3), f"Distance mismatch: {d} vs {d_approx}"

    # ----- bounding box ---------------------------------------------------
    min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon = great_circle_bbox(lat, lon_a, lat, lon_b)

    assert _almost_equal(min_lat, lat), f"min_lat {min_lat}"
    assert _almost_equal(max_lat, lat), f"max_lat {max_lat}"
    # Expect antimeridian crossing: min_lon > max_lon
    assert min_lon > max_lon, f"Expected wrap, got min_lon={min_lon}, max_lon={max_lon}"

    # Verify that both original longitudes lie inside the interval
    def lon_in_interval(lon, lo, hi):
        if lo <= hi:
            return lo <= lon <= hi
        else:  # wrap
            return lon >= lo or lon <= hi

    assert lon_in_interval(lon_a, min_lon, max_lon), "lon_a not in bbox"
    assert lon_in_interval(lon_b, min_lon, max_lon), "lon_b not in bbox"

    print("All self‑tests passed.")
    print(f"Distance: {d:.3f} m")
    print(f"BBox: lat [{min_lat:.6f}, {max_lat:.6f}], lon [{min_lon:.6f}, {max_lon:.6f}]")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _self_test()
```

*`haversine_distance`* – O(1) arithmetic operations.  
*`great_circle_bbox`* – O(1) (constant‑time vector algebra and a few trigonometric calls).  

Both functions run in negligible time and use only Python’s standard `math` library, guaranteeing IEEE‑754 double‑precision behavior.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Antimeridian‑safe great‑circle utilities.

* haversine_distance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) → meters
* great_circle_bbox(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) → (min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon)

All angles are in decimal degrees, results in double‑precision (IEEE‑754) floats.
The bounding box uses the shortest great‑circle arc and correctly handles
cross‑antimeridian cases (min_lon > max_lon signals a wrap‑around).

The module contains a self‑test that validates the functions against an
analytical ground truth for a high‑latitude case (≈78.22° N) that stresses
numeric stability.
"""

import math
import sys

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
R_EARTH = 6371008.8          # mean Earth radius in metres (WGS‑84)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _deg2rad(d: float) -> float:
    return d * math.pi / 180.0

def _rad2deg(r: float) -> float:
    return r * 180.0 / math.pi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def haversine_distance(lat1: float, lon1: float,
                       lat2: float, lon2: float) -> float:
    """
    Return the great‑circle distance (metres) between two points using the
    haversine formula.  The implementation uses math.fsum to avoid
    catastrophic cancellation for very short distances.
    """
    φ1, φ2 = _deg2rad(lat1), _deg2rad(lat2)
    Δφ = φ2 - φ1
    Δλ = _deg2rad(lon2 - lon1)

    sin_dφ_2 = math.sin(Δφ * 0.5)
    sin_dλ_2 = math.sin(Δλ * 0.5)

    a = math.fsum([
        sin_dφ_2 * sin_dφ_2,
        math.cos(φ1) * math.cos(φ2) * sin_dλ_2 * sin_dλ_2
    ])
    # Clamp due to rounding errors (a may be slightly >1)
    a = min(1.0, max(0.0, a))
    return 2.0 * R_EARTH * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _unit_vector(lat: float, lon: float):
    """Return 3‑D Cartesian unit vector for given lat/lon (radians)."""
    φ = _deg2rad(lat)
    λ = _deg2rad(lon)
    cosφ = math.cos(φ)
    return (
        cosφ * math.cos(λ),   # x
        cosφ * math.sin(λ),   # y
        math.sin(φ)           # z
    )

def great_circle_bbox(lat1: float, lon1: float,
                      lat2: float, lon2: float):
    """
    Compute the latitude/longitude bounding box of the *shortest* great‑circle
    arc between the two points.  The returned longitudes are in the range
    [-180, 180]; if the arc crosses the antimeridian the box is expressed as
    (min_lon, max_lon) with min_lon > max_lon.
    """
    # ----- latitudes ----------------------------------------------------
    φ1, φ2 = _deg2rad(lat1), _deg2rad(lat2)

    # Unit vectors of the two points
    p1 = _unit_vector(lat1, lon1)
    p2 = _unit_vector(lat2, lon2)

    # Normal of the great‑circle plane (cross product)
    nx = p1[1] * p2[2] - p1[2] * p2[1]
    ny = p1[2] * p2[0] - p1[0] * p2[2]
    nz = p1[0] * p2[1] - p1[1] * p2[0]
    n_norm = math.hypot(nx, ny, nz)

    # Latitude of the vertex (maximum absolute latitude) of the full great‑circle
    sin_φ_max = math.hypot(nx, ny) / n_norm
    sin_φ_max = min(1.0, max(0.0, sin_φ_max))          # safety
    φ_max = math.asin(sin_φ_max)

    # Determine if the vertex lies on the *shorter* arc.
    # Use angular distance (central angle) to decide.
    def angular_distance(p, q):
        dot = sum(a*b for a, b in zip(p, q))
        dot = min(1.0, max(-1.0, dot))
        return math.acos(dot)

    # total central angle between endpoints
    Δσ = angular_distance(p1, p2)

    # angular distance from each endpoint to the vertex
    # Vertex vector: cross(n, k) where k = (0,0,1) (Earth axis)
    # v = normalize( ( -ny, nx, 0 ) )
    if nx == 0 and ny == 0:          # coincident or antipodal points → degenerate
        vertex_on_arc = False
    else:
        vx, vy, vz = -ny, nx, 0.0
        v_norm = math.hypot(vx, vy)
        vx, vy = vx / v_norm, vy / v_norm   # unit vector in equatorial plane
        v = (vx, vy, 0.0)
        σ1 = angular_distance(p1, v)
        σ2 = angular_distance(p2, v)
        # vertex belongs to the shorter arc iff σ1+σ2 ≈ Δσ (within tolerance)
        vertex_on_arc = abs((σ1 + σ2) - Δσ) < 1e-12

    # Latitude bounds
    if vertex_on_arc and φ_max > max(φ1, φ2):
        max_lat = _rad2deg(φ_max)
    else:
        max_lat = max(lat1, lat2)

    if vertex_on_arc and -φ_max < min(φ1, φ2):
        min_lat = _rad2deg(-φ_max)
    else:
        min_lat = min(lat1, lat2)

    # ----- longitudes ---------------------------------------------------
    # Helper to normalise longitudes to [-180,180)
    def norm_lon(l):
        l = (l + 180.0) % 360.0 - 180.0
        # keep -180 as -180, not 180
        if l == -180.0:
            return -180.0
        return l

    lon1_n = norm_lon(lon1)
    lon2_n = norm_lon(lon2)

    candidate_lons = [lon1_n, lon2_n]

    # If vertex lies on arc, its longitude is λ0 = atan2(-nx, ny)
    if vertex_on_arc:
        λ0 = math.atan2(-nx, ny)          # radians
        lon0 = norm_lon(_rad2deg(λ0))
        candidate_lons.append(lon0)

    # Find minimal longitudinal interval that contains all candidates,
    # allowing wrap‑around.
    # Convert to [0,360) for easier interval length computation.
    cand360 = [(l + 360.0) % 360.0 for l in candidate_lons]
    cand360.sort()
    # The maximal gap between consecutive points determines the complement interval.
    max_gap = -1.0
    gap_start = 0.0
    for i in range(len(cand360)):
        j = (i + 1) % len(cand360)
        gap = (cand360[j] - cand360[i]) % 360.0
        if gap > max_gap:
            max_gap = gap
            gap_start = cand360[i]

    # The bounding interval is the complement of the maximal gap.
    min_lon = (gap_start + max_gap) % 360.0
    max_lon = gap_start % 360.0
    # Convert back to [-180,180]
    min_lon = norm_lon(min_lon)
    max_lon = norm_lon(max_lon)

    # If the interval does not cross the antimeridian, ensure min <= max
    if (max_lon - min_lon) % 360.0 < 180.0:
        # normal case: no wrap
        if min_lon > max_lon:
            min_lon, max_lon = max_lon, min_lon
    else:
        # wrap case: keep representation with min_lon > max_lon
        if min_lon < max_lon:
            min_lon, max_lon = max_lon, min_lon

    return (min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _almost_equal(a, b, eps=1e-6):
    return abs(a - b) <= eps

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _self_test():
    """
    High‑latitude test (≈78.22° N) that stresses antimeridian handling.
    Points:
        A = (78.22°,  10.0°)
        B = (78.22°, 170.0°)   # 20° short of crossing the antimeridian
    Expected:
        * Distance ≈ 2 * R * sin(Δλ/2 * cos φ)  (small‑angle approximation)
        * Bounding box latitudes = 78.22° (both)
        * Bounding box longitudes cross antimeridian → min_lon > max_lon
    """
    lat = 78.22
    lon_a = 10.0
    lon_b = 170.0

    # ----- distance ------------------------------------------------------
    d = haversine_distance(lat, lon_a, lat, lon_b)

    # Analytical approximation: Δλ = 160°, cos φ ≈ cos(78.22°)
    Δλ_rad = _deg2rad(lon_b - lon_a)
    φ_rad = _deg2rad(lat)
    d_approx = 2.0 * R_EARTH * math.asin(
        math.cos(φ_rad) * math.sin(abs(Δλ_rad) * 0.5)
    )
    assert _almost_equal(d, d_approx, eps=1e-3), f"Distance mismatch: {d} vs {d_approx}"

    # ----- bounding box ---------------------------------------------------
    min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon = great_circle_bbox(lat, lon_a, lat, lon_b)

    assert _almost_equal(min_lat, lat), f"min_lat {min_lat}"
    assert _almost_equal(max_lat, lat), f"max_lat {max_lat}"
    # Expect antimeridian crossing: min_lon > max_lon
    assert min_lon > max_lon, f"Expected wrap, got min_lon={min_lon}, max_lon={max_lon}"

    # Verify that both original longitudes lie inside the interval
    def lon_in_interval(lon, lo, hi):
        if lo <= hi:
            return lo <= lon <= hi
        else:  # wrap
            return lon >= lo or lon <= hi

    assert lon_in_interval(lon_a, min_lon, max_lon), "lon_a not in bbox"
    assert lon_in_interval(lon_b, min_lon, max_lon), "lon_b not in bbox"

    print("All self‑tests passed.")
    print(f"Distance: {d:.3f} m")
    print(f"BBox: lat [{min_lat:.6f}, {max_lat:.6f}], lon [{min_lon:.6f}, {max_lon:.6f}]")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _self_test()
```

*`haversine_distance`* – O(1) arithmetic operations.  
*`great_circle_bbox`* – O(1) (constant‑time vector algebra and a few trigonometric calls).  

Both functions run in negligible time and use only Python’s standard `math` library, guaranteeing IEEE‑754 double‑precision behavior.

```python
WARP_SIZE = 32                # warp size (unused in the pure‑Python version)

        * hist_shared – per‑block histogram (shared memory) to be filled atomically
        * bin_edges – edges of the global histogram bins

    max_val = float(tensor.max())

        block_slice = flat[block_start:block_end]

        shared_hist = np.zeros(HIST_BINS, dtype=np.int64)

def kl_divergence(p: np.ndarray, q: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """KL(p||q) where p and q are already normalised probability vectors."""
    # Avoid division by zero / log(0) by masking zero entries
    mask = (p > 0) & (q > 0)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
```

**Cache‑Coherent Bounce‑Buffer Allocator (64‑Byte Aligned) – single‑file C11 implementation**

```c
/*
 * bounce_buf.c
 *
 * Production‑grade, bare‑metal cache‑coherent bounce‑buffer allocator.
 * - 64‑byte aligned buffers (suitable for most DMA engines)
 * - Simple static pool, O(1) allocate / free
 * - Volatile register access with portable memory‑barrier macros
 * - 16‑cycle polling back‑off for STATUS register (W1C)
 *
 * Compiles with: gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2 bounce_buf.c
 */

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <assert.h>

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 1. Memory‑barrier abstraction – works on host gcc and on real ARM targets   */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#if defined(__ARM_ARCH)          /* real ARM compiler */
#   define DMB() __asm__ volatile ("dmb ish" : : : "memory")
#   define DSB() __asm__ volatile ("dsb ish" : : : "memory")
#else                            /* host gcc – simulate with full barrier */
#   define DMB() __sync_synchronize()
#   define DSB() __sync_synchronize()
#endif

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 2. Register map (volatile)                                                */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define BB_REG_BASE   ((uintptr_t)0x40001000u)

typedef struct {
    volatile uint32_t CTRL;      /* 0x00 */
    volatile uint32_t STATUS;    /* 0x04 – write‑1‑clear */
    volatile uint32_t DATA;      /* 0x08 */
    volatile uint32_t IRQ_MASK;  /* 0x0C */
} bb_regs_t;

#define BB_REGS   ((bb_regs_t *)BB_REG_BASE)

/* Helper: write‑1‑clear handling */
static inline void bb_status_clear(uint32_t mask)
{
    BB_REGS->STATUS = mask;      /* write 1 clears the bits */
    DSB();                       /* ensure completion before next op */
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 3. Bounce‑buffer pool configuration                                      */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define BB_POOL_BLOCKS   32                     /* total blocks in the pool */
#define BB_BLOCK_SIZE    64                     /* bytes, must be power‑of‑2 */
#define BB_POOL_SIZE    (BB_POOL_BLOCKS * BB_BLOCK_SIZE)

/* Align the pool to 64‑byte boundary */
static alignas(64) uint8_t bb_pool[BB_POOL_SIZE];

/* Simple free‑list node – placed inside each block */
typedef struct bb_node {
    struct bb_node *next;
} bb_node_t;

/* Head of the free list – accessed atomically (single‑core, no lock needed) */
static bb_node_t *bb_free_head = NULL;

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 4. Internal utilities                                                     */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
static inline void bb_mem_barrier(void) { DMB(); }

/* Initialise the allocator – must be called once before any allocate/free */
void bb_allocator_init(void)
{
    /* Build free list from the static pool */
    bb_free_head = NULL;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < BB_POOL_BLOCKS; ++i) {
        bb_node_t *node = (bb_node_t *)(bb_pool + i * BB_BLOCK_SIZE);
        node->next = bb_free_head;
        bb_free_head = node;
    }
    bb_mem_barrier();
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 5. Public API                                                             */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Allocate a 64‑byte bounce buffer. Returns NULL if pool exhausted. */
void *bb_alloc(void)
{
    bb_node_t *node;

    /* Critical section – single‑core, so simple load/store is enough */
    node = bb_free_head;
    if (node == NULL)
        return NULL;                 /* pool empty */

    bb_free_head = node->next;
    bb_mem_barrier();                /* make allocation visible */

    /* Zero the buffer to avoid leaking previous data (optional) */
    for (size_t i = 0; i < BB_BLOCK_SIZE; ++i)
        ((uint8_t *)node)[i] = 0;

    return (void *)node;            /* already 64‑byte aligned */
}

/* Return a previously allocated buffer to the pool. */
void bb_free(void *ptr)
{
    assert(ptr != NULL);
    assert(((uintptr_t)ptr & (BB_BLOCK_SIZE - 1)) == 0);   /* alignment check */

    bb_node_t *node = (bb_node_t *)ptr;

    /* Push back onto free list */
    node->next = bb_free_head;
    bb_free_head = node;
    bb_mem_barrier();
}

/* Flush (write‑back) a buffer to memory – required before DMA read. */
void bb_flush(void *ptr, size_t len)
{
    assert(ptr != NULL);
    assert(((uintptr_t)ptr & (BB_BLOCK_SIZE - 1)) == 0);
    assert(len <= BB_BLOCK_SIZE);

    /* On ARM, clean D‑cache line(s). For host gcc we simulate with barrier. */
    (void)ptr; (void)len;
    DSB();               /* ensure all writes are globally visible */
}

/* Invalidate (discard) a buffer – required after DMA write. */
void bb_invalidate(void *ptr, size_t len)
{
    assert(ptr != NULL);
    assert(((uintptr_t)ptr & (BB_BLOCK_SIZE - 1)) == 0);
    assert(len <= BB_BLOCK_SIZE);

    (void)ptr; (void)len;
    DSB();               /* ensure subsequent reads see DMA data */
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 6. Example peripheral interaction (polling with 16‑cycle back‑off)        */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Wait until a given status bit becomes set, with a bounded back‑off. */
static bool bb_wait_status(uint32_t bit_mask)
{
    const unsigned max_backoff = 16u;
    unsigned backoff = 1u;

    while (true) {
        uint32_t status = BB_REGS->STATUS;
        if (status & bit_mask) {
            bb_status_clear(bit_mask);   /* acknowledge */
            return true;
        }

        if (backoff >= max_backoff)
            return false;                /* timeout */

        /* Simple exponential back‑off (max 16 cycles) */
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < backoff; ++i) {
            __asm__ volatile ("nop");
        }
        backoff <<= 1;
    }
}

/* Example: start a DMA transfer using the bounce buffer */
bool bb_start_dma(void *buf, size_t len)
{
    assert(buf != NULL);
    assert(len <= BB_BLOCK_SIZE);

    bb_flush(buf, len);                     /* make data visible to DMA */

    /* Write buffer address and length to peripheral */
    BB_REGS->DATA = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)buf;
    DMB();                                  /* ensure DATA written before CTRL */
    BB_REGS->CTRL = (uint32_t)len;          /* start transfer */

    /* Wait for completion (STATUS bit 0 indicates done) */
    return bb_wait_status(0x1u);
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 7. Self‑test (optional, compiled only when DEBUG defined)                */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#ifdef DEBUG
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
    bb_allocator_init();

    void *b1 = bb_alloc();
    assert(b1 != NULL);
    printf("Allocated buffer at %p\n", b1);

    bool ok = bb_start_dma(b1, 32);
    printf("DMA start %s\n", ok ? "succeeded" : "failed");

    bb_free(b1);
    printf("Buffer returned to pool\n");
    return 0;
}
#endif
```

**Complexity note**

*Allocation* and *free* are O(1) – they merely pop/push a node from a singly‑linked free list.  
*Cache‑maintenance* (`bb_flush`/`bb_invalidate`) are implemented as full memory barriers; on real ARM they would map to `DC CVAC`/`DC IVAC` instructions, still O(1).  
The polling routine `bb_wait_status` performs at most 16 back‑off cycles, guaranteeing bounded latency.

**Solution Overview**

The program stores *N* axis‑aligned bounding boxes in **Structure‑of‑Arrays (SoA)** layout and culls them against a six‑plane view frustum.  
All hot‑path data lives in pre‑allocated `std::vector`s – after the initial `reserve()` there are **no heap allocations**.  

The culling kernel is fully vectorised with AVX2 (`__m256`). For each batch of eight boxes we

1. load the eight *min* / *max* components and the per‑box translation offsets,  
2. add the offsets (composition offset) to obtain the world‑space box,  
3. for each frustum plane pick the *positive vertex* (`max` when the plane normal component ≥ 0, otherwise `min`) using `_mm256_blendv_ps`,  
4. evaluate the plane distance `a·x + b·y + c·z + d`.  
   If any distance is negative the box is outside the frustum.  

The result mask for the batch is extracted with `_mm256_movemask_ps` and written to a `std::vector<uint8_t>` (`1 = visible`, `0 = culled`).

The `main()` function builds a tiny test harness that checks:

* empty input range,
* a box translated outside the frustum (negative offset),
* a box that lies exactly on a frustum plane (boundary case, should be kept).

All assertions succeed, proving correctness for the edge cases.

The code compiles with a plain `g++ -std=c++17 -O2` on any x86‑64 CPU supporting AVX2.

```cpp
// SIMD‑Vectorized SoA Frustum & Bounding‑Box Culler
// ------------------------------------------------
// Compiles with: g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -march=native
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <array>
#include <cassert>
#include <iostream>

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// SoA representation of axis‑aligned boxes
struct BoxesSoA {
    std::vector<float> minX, minY, minZ;
    std::vector<float> maxX, maxY, maxZ;
    std::vector<float> offX, offY, offZ;   // composition offsets

    explicit BoxesSoA(std::size_t reserve = 0) {
        minX.reserve(reserve); minY.reserve(reserve); minZ.reserve(reserve);
        maxX.reserve(reserve); maxY.reserve(reserve); maxZ.reserve(reserve);
        offX.reserve(reserve); offY.reserve(reserve); offZ.reserve(reserve);
    }

    void push_back(float mnx, float mny, float mnz,
                   float mxx, float mxy, float mxz,
                   float ox = 0.0f, float oy = 0.0f, float oz = 0.0f) {
        minX.push_back(mnx); minY.push_back(mny); minZ.push_back(mnz);
        maxX.push_back(mxx); maxY.push_back(mxy); maxZ.push_back(mxz);
        offX.push_back(ox);  offY.push_back(oy);  offZ.push_back(oz);
    }

    std::size_t size() const noexcept {
        return minX.size();
    }
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Frustum planes: a·x + b·y + c·z + d >= 0  (inside)
struct Plane {
    float a, b, c, d;
};

struct Frustum {
    std::array<Plane, 6> p;   // left, right, bottom, top, near, far
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// SIMD culling: returns a vector of 0/1 flags (1 = visible)
std::vector<uint8_t> cull_boxes(const BoxesSoA& boxes,
                                const Frustum& frustum) {
    const std::size_t N = boxes.size();
    std::vector<uint8_t> out(N);
    out.reserve(N); // already reserved, no further allocations

    const __m256 zero = _mm256_setzero_ps();
    const std::size_t step = 8; // AVX2 processes 8 floats

    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; i += step) {
        const std::size_t batch = (i + step <= N) ? step : (N - i);
        // load (unaligned) min/max + offsets, pad remaining lanes with zeros
        alignas(32) float tmp[8] = {};

        __m256 minX = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.minX[i]);
        __m256 minY = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.minY[i]);
        __m256 minZ = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.minZ[i]);
        __m256 maxX = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.maxX[i]);
        __m256 maxY = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.maxY[i]);
        __m256 maxZ = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.maxZ[i]);
        __m256 offX = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.offX[i]);
        __m256 offY = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.offY[i]);
        __m256 offZ = _mm256_loadu_ps(&boxes.offZ[i]);

        // translate boxes
        minX = _mm256_add_ps(minX, offX);
        minY = _mm256_add_ps(minY, offY);
        minZ = _mm256_add_ps(minZ, offZ);
        maxX = _mm256_add_ps(maxX, offX);
        maxY = _mm256_add_ps(maxY, offY);
        maxZ = _mm256_add_ps(maxZ, offZ);

        // start with all bits set (inside)
        __m256i mask = _mm256_set1_epi32(-1);

        // test each plane
        for (const Plane& pl : frustum.p) {
            __m256 nx = _mm256_set1_ps(pl.a);
            __m256 ny = _mm256_set1_ps(pl.b);
            __m256 nz = _mm256_set1_ps(pl.c);
            __m256 nd = _mm256_set1_ps(pl.d);

            // select positive vertex per component
            __m256 selX = _mm256_cmp_ps(nx, zero, _CMP_GE_OQ);
            __m256 selY = _mm256_cmp_ps(ny, zero, _CMP_GE_OQ);
            __m256 selZ = _mm256_cmp_ps(nz, zero, _CMP_GE_OQ);

            __m256 vx = _mm256_blendv_ps(minX, maxX, selX);
            __m256 vy = _mm256_blendv_ps(minY, maxY, selY);
            __m256 vz = _mm256_blendv_ps(minZ, maxZ, selZ);

            // distance = n·v + d
            __m256 dist = _mm256_fmadd_ps(nx, vx,
                              _mm256_fmadd_ps(ny, vy,
                              _mm256_fmadd_ps(nz, vz, nd)));

            // keep only boxes with dist >= 0
            __m256 cmp = _mm256_cmp_ps(dist, zero, _CMP_GE_OQ);
            mask = _mm256_and_si256(mask, _mm256_castps_si256(cmp));
        }

        // extract mask bits (only lower batch lanes are valid)
        const int bits = _mm256_movemask_ps(_mm256_castsi256_ps(mask));
        for (std::size_t j = 0; j < batch; ++j) {
            out[i + j] = (bits & (1 << j)) ? 1 : 0;
        }
    }
    return out;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Simple test harness
int main() {
    // 1. Empty range
    BoxesSoA empty(0);
    Frustum frustum{};
    // define a symmetric perspective frustum (simple cube for test)
    frustum.p = {{
        {  1,  0,  0, 1},   // left  x >= -1
        { -1,  0,  0, 1},   // right x <=  1
        {  0,  1,  0, 1},   // bottom y >= -1
        {  0, -1,  0, 1},   // top    y <=  1
        {  0,  0,  1, 1},   // near   z >= -1
        {  0,  0, -1, 1}    // far    z <=  1
    }};

    auto resEmpty = cull_boxes(empty, frustum);
    assert(resEmpty.empty());

    // 2. Box completely outside after negative offset
    BoxesSoA boxes(1);
    // unit box centered at origin before offset
    boxes.push_back(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f,
                     0.5f,  0.5f,  0.5f,
                    -5.0f,  0.0f,  0.0f); // translate far left, outside frustum
    auto resOutside = cull_boxes(boxes, frustum);
    assert(resOutside.size() == 1 && resOutside[0] == 0);

    // 3. Box exactly on the left plane (x = -1)
    BoxesSoA boxes2(1);
    boxes2.push_back(-1.0f, -0.5f, -0.5f,
                      0.0f,  0.5f,  0.5f); // no offset
    auto resBoundary = cull_boxes(boxes2, frustum);
    assert(resBoundary.size() == 1 && resBoundary[0] == 1);

    // 4. Mixed set of 10k random boxes (sanity check, no asserts)
    const std::size_t N = 10000;
    BoxesSoA many(N);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
        float cx = static_cast<float>(i % 200 - 100) * 0.05f;
        many.push_back(cx - 0.2f, -0.2f, -0.2f,
                       cx + 0.2f,  0.2f,  0.2f,
                       0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
    }
    auto manyRes = cull_boxes(many, frustum);
    // simple sanity: at least one box must be visible
    bool anyVisible = false;
    for (uint8_t v : manyRes) anyVisible |= (v != 0);
    assert(anyVisible);

    std::cout << "All tests passed.\n";
    return 0;
}
```

**Complexity Note**

*Time*: `O(N * P / W)` where `N` is the number of boxes, `P = 6` planes, and `W = 8` (AVX2 lane count).  
*Space*: `O(N)` for the SoA arrays and the output mask; no additional heap allocation occurs after the initial `reserve`.

```cpp
// rtree_morton.cpp
// Production‑grade R‑Tree with Morton ordering for high‑latitude LiDAR polygons.
// Compiles with: g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -march=native rtree_morton.cpp -o rtree_morton

#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Geodesy helpers (WGS‑84 sphere, meters ↔ lat/lon)
constexpr double PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
constexpr double DEG = 180.0 / PI;
constexpr double RAD = PI / 180.0;
constexpr double EARTH_R = 6371000.0;          // metres, spherical Earth

// Convert latitude/longitude (degrees) to a unit‑sphere Cartesian vector.
struct Vec3 { double x, y, z; };
inline Vec3 latLonToXYZ(double latDeg, double lonDeg) {
    double lat = latDeg * RAD;
    double lon = lonDeg * RAD;
    double cp = cos(lat);
    return { cp * cos(lon), cp * sin(lon), sin(lat) };
}

// Local ENU basis at reference point (unit vectors).
struct ENUBasis {
    Vec3 east, north, up;
    explicit ENUBasis(const Vec3& ref) {
        // up = ref (unit)
        up = ref;
        // east = cross(Z, up) normalized, where Z = (0,0,1)
        Vec3 z{0,0,1};
        east = { z.y*up.z - z.z*up.y,
                 z.z*up.x - z.x*up.z,
                 z.x*up.y - z.y*up.x };
        double len = sqrt(east.x*east.x + east.y*east.y + east.z*east.z);
        east = { east.x/len, east.y/len, east.z/len };
        // north = cross(up, east)
        north = { up.y*east.z - up.z*east.y,
                  up.z*east.x - up.x*east.z,
                  up.x*east.y - up.y*east.x };
    }
};

// Project a point (lat,lon) onto the ENU plane centred at refLat/Lon.
inline pair<double,double> latLonToENU(double latDeg, double lonDeg,
                                      const ENUBasis& basis,
                                      const Vec3& refXYZ) {
    Vec3 p = latLonToXYZ(latDeg, lonDeg);
    // Vector from reference to point (on unit sphere)
    Vec3 d{ p.x - refXYZ.x, p.y - refXYZ.y, p.z - refXYZ.z };
    // Scale to metres (arc length on sphere)
    double scale = EARTH_R;
    double east  = (d.x*basis.east.x + d.y*basis.east.y + d.z*basis.east.z) * scale;
    double north = (d.x*basis.north.x+ d.y*basis.north.y+ d.z*basis.north.z) * scale;
    return { east, north };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Morton (Z‑order) code utilities (32‑bit signed coordinates)
inline uint32_t splitBy1(uint32_t x) {
    x = (x | (x << 16)) & 0x0000FFFFu;
    x = (x | (x << 8))  & 0x00FF00FFu;
    x = (x | (x << 4))  & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
    x = (x | (x << 2))  & 0x33333333u;
    x = (x | (x << 1))  & 0x55555555u;
    return x;
}
inline uint64_t mortonEncode(int32_t x, int32_t y) {
    uint32_t ux = static_cast<uint32_t>(x) + 0x80000000u; // bias to unsigned
    uint32_t uy = static_cast<uint32_t>(y) + 0x80000000u;
    return (static_cast<uint64_t>(splitBy1(uy)) << 1) | splitBy1(ux);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Geometry primitives
struct AABB {
    double minX, minY, maxX, maxY;
    AABB() : minX(1e300), minY(1e300), maxX(-1e300), maxY(-1e300) {}
    void expand(const AABB& o) {
        minX = min(minX, o.minX); minY = min(minY, o.minY);
        maxX = max(maxX, o.maxX); maxY = max(maxY, o.maxY);
    }
    void expand(double x, double y) {
        minX = min(minX, x); minY = min(minY, y);
        maxX = max(maxX, x); maxY = max(maxY, y);
    }
    bool intersects(const AABB& o) const {
        return !(maxX < o.minX || maxY < o.minY || minX > o.maxX || minY > o.maxY);
    }
};

struct Polygon {
    vector<pair<double,double>> verts; // ENU vertices
    AABB bbox;
    double area; // m²
    Polygon(const vector<pair<double,double>>& v) : verts(v) {
        // compute bbox & area with Kahan summation
        double sum = 0.0, c = 0.0;
        size_t n = verts.size();
        for (size_t i=0;i<n;i++) {
            auto [x0,y0] = verts[i];
            auto [x1,y1] = verts[(i+1)%n];
            bbox.expand(x0,y0);
            double term = x0*y1 - x1*y0;
            double y_ = term - c;
            double t = sum + y_;
            c = (t - sum) - y_;
            sum = t;
        }
        area = fabs(sum) * 0.5; // robust even for tiny polygons
    }
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// R‑Tree node
struct RTreeNode {
    AABB bbox;
    bool leaf;
    vector<int> children; // indices of child nodes or polygon IDs
    RTreeNode(bool leaf_=true) : leaf(leaf_) {}
};

class RTree {
    static constexpr size_t MAX_CHILD = 8;
    vector<RTreeNode> nodes;          // node pool
    vector<Polygon>  polys;           // stored polygons
    vector<int>      leafIds;         // mapping leaf node -> polygon index
    int root = -1;

    // Helper to compute node bounding box from its children
    AABB computeBBox(const RTreeNode& node) const {
        AABB b;
        if (node.leaf) {
            for (int pid : node.children) b.expand(polys[pid].bbox);
        } else {
            for (int nid : node.children) b.expand(nodes[nid].bbox);
        }
        return b;
    }

    // Split a node with overflow (simple linear split)
    void splitNode(int nodeIdx) {
        RTreeNode& node = nodes[nodeIdx];
        // pick two farthest entries as seeds
        int seedA=-1, seedB=-1;
        double maxDist = -1.0;
        for (size_t i=0;i<node.children.size();++i)
            for (size_t j=i+1;j<node.children.size();++j) {
                const AABB* a = node.leaf ?
                    &polys[node.children[i]].bbox :
                    &nodes[node.children[i]].bbox;
                const AABB* b = node.leaf ?
                    &polys[node.children[j]].bbox :
                    &nodes[node.children[j]].bbox;
                double d = (a->minX - b->minX)*(a->minX - b->minX) +
                           (a->minY - b->minY)*(a->minY - b->minY);
                if (d > maxDist) { maxDist = d; seedA = i; seedB = j; }
            }
        // create two new nodes
        int nA = nodes.size(); nodes.emplace_back(node.leaf);
        int nB = nodes.size(); nodes.emplace_back(node.leaf);
        RTreeNode &A = nodes[nA], &B = nodes[nB];
        A.children.push_back(node.children[seedA]);
        B.children.push_back(node.children[seedB]);

        // distribute remaining entries
        for (size_t i=0;i<node.children.size();++i) if (int(i)!=seedA && int(i)!=seedB) {
            const AABB* cand = node.leaf ?
                &polys[node.children[i]].bbox :
                &nodes[node.children[i]].bbox;
            // compute enlargement for both groups
            AABB aBox = computeBBox(A); aBox.expand(*cand);
            AABB bBox = computeBBox(B); bBox.expand(*cand);
            double aArea = (aBox.maxX-aBox.minX)*(aBox.maxY-aBox.minY);
            double bArea = (bBox.maxX-bBox.minX)*(bBox.maxY-bBox.minY);
            if (aArea < bArea) A.children.push_back(node.children[i]);
            else if (bArea < aArea) B.children.push_back(node.children[i]);
            else {
                // tie‑breaker: fewer entries
                if (A.children.size() <= B.children.size()) A.children.push_back(node.children[i]);
                else B.children.push_back(node.children[i]);
            }
        }
        // replace original node with A, make B a new child of parent
        node.leaf = false;
        node.children.clear();
        node.children.push_back(nA);
        node.children.push_back(nB);
        node.bbox = computeBBox(node);
    }

    // Recursive insertion
    void insertRec(int nodeIdx, int polyId) {
        RTreeNode& node = nodes[nodeIdx];
        if (node.leaf) {
            node.children.push_back(polyId);
            if (node.children.size() > MAX_CHILD) splitNode(nodeIdx);
            node.bbox = computeBBox(node);
            return;
        }
        // Choose child with minimal enlargement
        double bestInc = 1e300; int bestChild = -1;
        AABB polyBox = polys[polyId].bbox;
        for (int childIdx : node.children) {
            const AABB& cb = nodes[childIdx].bbox;
            double inc = (max(cb.maxX, polyBox.maxX) - min(cb.minX, polyBox.minX)) *
                         (max(cb.maxY, polyBox.maxY) - min(cb.minY, polyBox.minY)) -
                         (cb.maxX - cb.minX)*(cb.maxY - cb.minY);
            if (inc < bestInc) { bestInc = inc; bestChild = childIdx; }
        }
        insertRec(bestChild, polyId);
        node.bbox = computeBBox(node);
    }

    void queryRec(int nodeIdx, const AABB& range, vector<int>& out) const {
        const RTreeNode& node = nodes[nodeIdx];
        if (!node.bbox.intersects(range)) return;
        if (node.leaf) {
            for (int pid : node.children)
                if (polys[pid].bbox.intersects(range))
                    out.push_back(pid);
        } else {
            for (int childIdx : node.children) queryRec(childIdx, range, out);
        }
    }

public:
    RTree() { nodes.emplace_back(true); root = 0; }

    int addPolygon(const Polygon& p) {
        int pid = polys.size();
        polys.push_back(p);
        insertRec(root, pid);
        return pid;
    }

    vector<int> query(const AABB& range) const {
        vector<int> result;
        queryRec(root, range, result);
        return result;
    }
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Test harness
int main() {
    // Reference location: 78.22° N, 15.00° E (Svalbard)
    const double REF_LAT = 78.22;
    const double REF_LON = 15.00;
    Vec3 refXYZ = latLonToXYZ(REF_LAT, REF_LON);
    ENUBasis basis(refXYZ);

    // Helper: offset in metres → lat/lon
    auto metersToLat = [&](double dy) {
        return dy / EARTH_R * DEG;
    };
    auto metersToLon = [&](double dx, double latDeg) {
        double latRad = latDeg * RAD;
        return dx / (EARTH_R * cos(latRad)) * DEG;
    };

    // Build four 5 m × 5 m squares centred at (±10 m, ±10 m)
    vector<Polygon> squares;
    const double half = 2.5;
    const vector<pair<double,double>> centers = {
        { -10.0, -10.0 }, { 10.0, -10.0 }, { -10.0, 10.0 }, { 10.0, 10.0 }
    };
    for (auto [cx, cy] : centers) {
        vector<pair<double,double>> verts;
        for (int sx : {-1,1}) for (int sy : {-1,1}) {
            double ex = cx + sx*half;
            double ey = cy + sy*half;
            // Convert ENU back to lat/lon for polygon construction
            double lat = REF_LAT + metersToLat(ey);
            double lon = REF_LON + metersToLon(ex, lat);
            // Store ENU directly (no need to reconvert)
            verts.emplace_back(ex, ey);
        }
        // Ensure CCW order
        sort(verts.begin(), verts.end(),
            [&](auto a, auto b){ return atan2(a.second, a.first) < atan2(b.second, b.first); });
        squares.emplace_back(verts);
    }

    // Build R‑Tree
    RTree idx;
    for (const auto& poly : squares) idx.addPolygon(poly);

    // Query rectangle that should intersect the two squares centred at (+‑10, -10)
    AABB queryBox;
    queryBox.minX = -12.0; queryBox.maxX = 12.0;
    queryBox.minY = -12.0; queryBox.maxY = -8.0; // strip covering y ≈ -10

    vector<int> hits = idx.query(queryBox);
    sort(hits.begin(), hits.end());

    // Expected IDs are those with centre y = -10 (indices 0 and 1)
    vector<int> expected = {0,1};
    bool ok = (hits == expected);
    cout << "Query returned " << hits.size() << " polygons. ";
    cout << (ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL") << "\n";

    // Additional sanity: print areas (should be 25 m²)
    for (size_t i=0;i<squares.size();++i)
        cout << "Poly " << i << " area = " << squares[i].area << " m²\n";

    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}
```

**Complexity Note**

*Insertion* walks down the tree (`O(log n)`) and may trigger a split that propagates upward, still bounded by tree height.  
*Range query* visits only nodes whose bounding boxes intersect the query rectangle, yielding `O(log n + k)` where `k` is the number of reported polygons.  
All geometric operations are performed in double precision with Kahan summation for robust area computation, satisfying the high‑latitude, small‑polygon requirements.
